quest:10.text:
The Scrimshank Redemption. In Gadgetzan, Fizzledowser seeks news of his missing assistant, Junior Surveyor Scrimshank. Scrimshank went into the Gaping Chasm, southeast of town. Now Fizzledowser asks you to find Scrimshank or the surveying equipment. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser has heard nothing from Junior Surveyor Scrimshank since he went into the Gaping Chasm. The last report from there spoke of more weird bugs. Fizzledowser wonders whether the bugs now hold two great regions of the desert.

He asks you to search for Scrimshank or, if Scrimshank is gone, the surveying equipment. Fizzledowser fears it may be all that remains.

quest:1052.text: Down the Scarlet Path. Brother Anton sends you from Desolace to Southshore with a sealed letter for Raleigh the Devout. Your deeds against the undead are only the beginning; Lordaeron holds the plague's true danger. Brother Anton takes pride in the Scarlet Crusade's strongholds in Lordaeron. The Crusade claims cleansing bastions from Hearthglen to Tirisfal Glades. Your work against the undead in Desolace has proven you, Anton says. Yet the plague's true danger lies in Lordaeron. Brother Anton sends you to Southshore, a town in the Eastern Kingdoms, to find Raleigh the Devout, a crusader. Anton seals a letter with his mark. He says Raleigh will give you an escort to a place of honor within the Scarlet Monastery.

quest:110.text: Insect Part Analysis. In Gadgetzan, Fizzledowser needs word on the insect parts sent to Alchemist Pestlezugg. With Scrimshank lost, the Senior Surveyor is sorting his surveying gear and personal effects. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser is putting Scrimshank's surveying gear and personal effects in order. He fears the bugs will claim more lives, so he sends you to Alchemist Pestlezugg in Gadgetzan. Learn whether Pestlezugg has finished processing the insect parts the surveyors sent. If they are ready, bring them back to Fizzledowser.

quest:1118.text: Back to Booty Bay. At the Mirage Raceway, Kravel Koalbeard sends you back to Booty Bay with a letter and asks you to keep his scheme quiet. It is risky, but success could bring you both a bundle. This follows Rumors for Kravel. At the Mirage Raceway, Kravel Koalbeard trusts you to finish a job and keep silent. His new scheme is risky, but success could bring you both a bundle. He sends you back to Booty Bay, where his last job took you, to find Crank Fizzlebub and deliver a letter. If Crank needs help, do your best. Kravel says the effort will be worth it.

quest:1119.text: Zanzil's Mixture and a Fool's Stout. At the Mirage Raceway, Kravel Koalbeard awaits a stout blended with Zanzil's Mixture. Crank Fizzlebub calls it Fool's Stout and believes Kravel needs it, so you carry it to him on the Shimmering Flats before it spoils. Crank Fizzlebub has blended Zanzil's Mixture into stout, making a potent drink he calls Fool's Stout. He believes Kravel needs it and wants to hear how it works. So you carry the drink to Kravel Koalbeard at the Mirage Raceway on the Shimmering Flats. Crank warns you not to keep the stout long. The mixture drives the yeast into high gear, and the drink will not stay fresh forever.

quest:1120.text: Get the Gnomes Drunk. At the Mirage Raceway, Get the Gnomes Drunk begins with a test of Fool's Stout on a pit crew. Kravel Koalbeard gives you the stout for the Gnome Pit Boss nearby and warns that it will go bad eventually. Kravel Koalbeard asks you to test Fool's Stout on one of the pit crews. Choose the gnomes, and he gives you the stout for the Gnome Pit Boss nearby at the Mirage Raceway. That choice tips the races toward the goblins. Kravel warns you not to wait too long, since the stout will go bad eventually.

quest:1121.text: Get the Goblins Drunk. At the Mirage Raceway, Kravel Koalbeard asks you to test Fool's Stout on a pit crew. Choose the goblins and carry the stout to the nearby Goblin Pit Boss before it goes bad. Kravel Koalbeard gives you Fool's Stout to test on one of the pit crews. If you choose the goblins, take it to the nearby Goblin Pit Boss at the Mirage Raceway. That choice tips the races toward the gnomes. The stout will go bad eventually, so Kravel warns you not to dawdle.

quest:1122.text: Report Back to Fizzlebub. Kravel Koalbeard reports that the Fool's Stout worked and sends you to Booty Bay with news for Crank Fizzlebub. He has bet on the next race and hopes the pit crew you made drunk wrecked their own car. This follows your choice to make one pit crew drunk. Kravel Koalbeard says the Fool's Stout worked well. He's bet on the next race and hopes the pit crew you made drunk wrecked their own car. Take his note about the successful test to Crank Fizzlebub in Booty Bay. Crank will want the news, and Kravel hopes to get more stout for future races.

quest:1127.text: Fool's Stout. In Booty Bay, travelers seek more Fool's Stout for the Shimmering Flats raceway. Crank Fizzlebub needs twelve flasks of Zanzil's mixture to brew another batch. Travelers bound for the gnomes at the raceway may find their Fool's Stout has expired before they arrive. In Booty Bay, Crank Fizzlebub can brew a replacement. The goblin needs twelve flasks of Zanzil's mixture, and offers compensation for fetching them, with a little extra for discretion.

quest:113.text:
Insect Part Analysis. From Tanaris, Alchemist Pestlezugg sends an urgent warning to Gadgetzan. The danger threatens both places and may spread across southern Kalimdor. Alchemist Pestlezugg asks you to carry the report to Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser in Gadgetzan. The danger threatens Tanaris and Gadgetzan, and may spread across southern Kalimdor. It could reach all of Azeroth, and nothing suggests it will subside. Pestlezugg wants everyone who can read to know.

Fizzledowser is to make a duplicate for you, so you can share it freely with your allegiance.

quest:1166.text: Overlord Mok'Morokk's Concern. Overlord Mok'Morokk sends you south from Brackenwall Village to recover what he left at the Stonemaul clan's old home. He wants his grog, snuff and strongbox back. Mok'Morokk says Rexxar made him the mighty leader of the Stonemaul clan. He says he keeps his people safe. When big dragons came to the clan's old home and brought fire, he found them a new home here in Dustwallow. Mok'Morokk left the old home in such a hurry that he forgot his grog, snuff and strongbox. He points you south to the Den of Flame and the Stonemaul Ruins, certain his things are there. He says he is too busy leading the ogres to go himself.

quest:1168.text: Army of the Black Dragon. In Brackenwall Village, the Army of the Black Dragon has left Tharg grieving and thirsting for vengeance. He blames Overlord Mok'Morokk for ordering the ogres to flee. Black dragons killed Tharg's wife along with many ogres. After Rexxar made Mok'Morokk Overlord, the new leader ordered the survivors to run until they reached Brackenwall Village. Tharg says ogres are poor at running and should fight instead. He believes Mok'Morokk thinks only of himself, though Mok'Morokk now tells all ogres to stay put and keep Brackenwall Village safe. Tharg calls the Stonemaul Ruins his home and likes the south. Brackenwall Village is no home to him. He wants revenge on the black dragon army and a return to the ruins, so he asks you to cut down Firemane Scouts and Firemane Ash Tails among its ranks.

quest:1169.text:
Identifying the Brood. In Brackenwall Village, Draz'Zilb seeks the beast that attacked the clan's old home. Draz'Zilb says Mok'Morokk clings to power while Tharg struggles with sorrow and vengeance, and asks you for fifteen searing tongues and fifteen searing hearts. Draz'Zilb says Mok'Morokk is consumed by power while Tharg wrestles with sorrow and a thirst for vengeance. In Draz'Zilb's view, no one else is trying to learn who attacked the clan's old home. The ogre speaks with care, though you might have expected a brute's words. Draz'Zilb asks you to take fifteen tongues and fifteen hearts from the whelps and hatchlings. The burned young belong to the black dragon army, and Draz'Zilb hopes their remains will reveal which beast sent her young into the ogres' home.

If the ogres learn what kind of beast they face, they may destroy their enemy for good and reclaim Stonemaul Village from ruin. Draz'Zilb says getting Mok'Morokk to leave the swamp will be a great labor of its own.

quest:1170.text: The Brood of Onyxia. Draz'Zilb fears Onyxia's brood has come for more than a siege against a few ogres. Draz'Zilb reports that Onyxia's brood has invaded Stonemaul Village. Onyxia is Deathwing's daughter, and her arrival troubles him. He is certain the brood seeks more than a siege against a few ogres. So you carry word to Overlord Mok'Morokk in Brackenwall Village, where he can take action.

quest:1171.text: The Brood of Onyxia. At Brackenwall Village, The Brood of Onyxia meets Overlord Mok'Morokk's denial. He says no black dragons are here and sends you back to Draz'Zilb with word that the ogres will stay. Overlord Mok'Morokk wants to be left alone after Draz'Zilb reports the brood of Onyxia. He says the ogres will stay where they are and denies that any black dragon is here. Carry his answer to Draz'Zilb in Brackenwall Village.

quest:1172.text: The Brood of Onyxia. In the marsh's south, Draz'Zilb sends you against Onyxia's eggs. No more of her whelps should hatch. Onyxia's brood lies scattered through the Dragonmurk. Draz'Zilb urges you south to the Wyrmbog, where the ogre is sure Onyxia made her lair and scattered her eggs. Dragons nest in the land around Stonemaul Village, keeping the ogres from taking it back. So you are sent to find and destroy the eggs.

quest:1173.text: Challenge Overlord Mok'Morokk. In Brackenwall Village, Overlord Mok'Morokk laughs at your challenge and vows to crush you. Draz'Zilb expected you to drive him from the village. After The Brood of Onyxia, you face Overlord Mok'Morokk. He laughs at your nerve and promises to crush you. Then he tells you to speak when you are ready for a beating. Draz'Zilb in Brackenwall Village expected you to chase Mok'Morokk from the village. Why have you returned only to talk?

quest:1187.text: Razzeric's Tweaking. On the Shimmering Flats, Razzeric's Tweaking gives racers more power once Pozzik is done with them. A seaforium booster ordered from Shreev in Gadgetzan traveled by zeppelin, which Razzeric says crashed in Dustwallow Marsh. He wants the booster brought back. Pozzik is a fine mechanic, Razzeric says, but too cautious with firepower and too ready to hold back. Once Pozzik finishes with a racer, Razzeric loosens its controls, removes parts of its frame, and adds power. He ordered a seaforium booster from Shreev at the Gizmorium in Gadgetzan. Razzeric says the zeppelin carrying it crashed in Dustwallow Marsh. The booster belongs back on the Shimmering Flats. Facing the track without that extra kick would be a travesty.

quest:1188.text: Safety First. Razzeric sends you south with a seaforium booster, bound for Shreev in Gadgetzan. Its safety is still on, though Razzeric asked for it to be removed. Razzeric finds the safety still on his seaforium booster. It limits the power the booster can deliver, though he had asked Shreev to remove it. So he gives you the booster and sends you south of the Shimmering Flats, into the Tanaris desert. Shreev can remove the safety at the Gadgetzan Gizmorium.

quest:1189.text: Safety First. On the Shimmering Flats, you carry Shreev’s modified seaforium booster back to Razzeric. Shreev warns that one slip while setting it off could leave Razzeric a scorch mark on the track. Shreev hands you the modified booster, prepared as Razzeric asked. He warns that Razzeric must take care when setting it off. One slip, and Razzeric will be a scorch mark on the track instead of racing ahead. Shreev says that would be a shame. Then he wonders whether the nineteenth driver would have been any good. Back on the Shimmering Flats, Razzeric grumbles that Pozzik loaded a bucket of sand onto his racer. How can he reach top speed with sand beneath the seat?

quest:1190.text: Keeping Pace. Pozzik suspects the Brassbolts brothers have found a new material for their cars. Their designs and run data are unchanged, yet the cars go faster. Rizzle Brassbolts keeps close to his plans, and Zamek can distract him so you can take them. This follows News for Fizzle. The Brassbolts brothers' cars have grown faster, and Pozzik can find only one explanation: a new building material. Their designs and the data from their runs remain unchanged. Rizzle Brassbolts has been absorbed in plans for this discovery almost constantly. Zamek can distract Rizzle while you take his plans. Pozzik is waiting for them on the Shimmering Flats.

quest:1191.text: Zamek's Distraction. In Thousand Needles, Zamek's Distraction can draw Rizzle away while you work through Keeping Pace. You cannot finish Keeping Pace without it. While you work through Keeping Pace, Zamek draws Rizzle from his hut. The Indurium plans remain behind.

quest:1192.text: Indurium Ore. Pozzik needs Indurium Ore to build several parts for the racers. The ore lies at the Uldaman dig in the Badlands, across the sea in Khaz Modan. Gnomes are already gathering their own supply, and Pozzik wants to keep pace. Pozzik asks you to bring him four pieces of raw Indurium Ore. You can find it at the Uldaman dig in the Badlands, across the sea in Khaz Modan. Gnomes are already gathering their own supply, and Pozzik wants some too. This comes after Rizzle's Schematics.

quest:1194.text: Rizzle's Schematics. After Keeping Pace, you carry a raw indurium sample to Pozzik on the Shimmering Flats. Rizzle's plans lie beneath the ore, and his notes trace it to the dwarves' dig at Uldaman in the Badlands. They also describe how well indurium resists heat. Rizzle's plans explain how to refine indurium ore. Scrawled notes trace its source to the dwarves' dig at Uldaman in the Badlands. Other notes describe the ore's resistance to heat. A lump of raw indurium holds the plans down, and you take the sample to Pozzik.

quest:1252.text: Lieutenant Paval Reethe. At the Shady Rest Inn, Lieutenant Paval Reethe's badge lies beneath the rubble, marked with Theramore's sign. Bring it to Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore. Ash and debris bury a badge in the Shady Rest Inn ruins. Beneath it, Lieutenant Paval Reethe's name lies below Theramore's sign. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore asks what you found, and the badge belongs in his hands.

quest:1258.text: ... and Bugs. Morgan Stern in Theramore is shaping a recipe that may become Stormwind's next food craze. He has the Mudrock tongues, but still needs pristine, unscarred legs from a giant crab. Morgan Stern needs each crab leg's shell to shape his dish's appearance. Every leg must be pristine and unscarred, yet an adult crab may have only one or two legs fit for his research. He needs many, and the Muckshells of Dustwallow Marsh will not do. Only crabs from the faraway Swamp of Sorrows suit the recipe, so you face a long journey.

quest:1259.text: Lieutenant Paval Reethe. In Theramore, Captain Garran Vimes asks you to learn who Lieutenant Paval Reethe is. Captain Garran Vimes does not recognize Lieutenant Paval Reethe's name. So he sends you to Adjutant Tesoran in Theramore, who keeps the guard's records of its people and equipment. Vimes expects those records to reveal who Reethe is.

quest:1261.text: Marg Speaks. Near Theramore, Marg's stolen pendant and unfinished duty still weigh on them. Marg asks you to find the muckshell that killed them, recover the jeweled pendant taken from Alliance soldiers, and carry it to Nazeer Bloodpike in Brackenwall Village. Alliance soldiers had made camp on the beach near Theramore. One wore a pendant set with more gems than a soldier could pay for. Marg slipped into the camp that night and stole it. On the way back to base, a muckshell crab-man killed Marg. Now Marg asks you to find the muckshell, recover the pendant, and bring it to Nazeer in Brackenwall Village.

quest:1262.text: Report to Zor. Nazeer Bloodpike sends you to Orgrimmar with Marg's jeweled pendant. Strange that common soldiers carried such a fine piece, he asks Zor Lonetree, who knows Alliance politics, to judge its history. Nazeer Bloodpike finds it strange that common soldiers carried a pendant so fine. Perhaps its owner was in disguise, or perhaps the soldiers stole it themselves. Either way, Nazeer judges it a noble's pendant. Its true owner must be found to unravel the mystery. Zor Lonetree in Orgrimmar knows much of Alliance politics and can tell whether Stormwind's nobility once claimed it.

quest:1380.text: Khan Hratha. At Gelkis Village, Uthek the Wise sends you against the Maraudine after your help against the Magram. Their leader, Khan Hratha, carries a piece of a key Uthek wants returned to him. The Gelkis need your help against the Maraudine, Uthek the Wise tells you. Their War Horn stands on a tall bluff in the Valley of Spears. Sound it, and Khan Hratha will answer. But first, you need a warhorn mouthpiece. Only trusted Maraudine centaur carry one, and they are rare. More centaur arrive when the horn sounds. Hratha comes last. Khan Hratha holds a piece of a key. Uthek wants you to bring it to Gelkis Village.

quest:1381.text: Khan Hratha. In Desolace, Warug sets his sights on Khan Hratha after the Gelkis Khan's death. He sends you to face the Maraudine Khan and return with the piece of a key he carries. Warug wants Khan Hratha, the Maraudine Khan, dead. A horn on a bluff in the Valley of Spears will draw him out, but first you need its mouthpiece from a Maraudine centaur. Sound the horn and Maraudine centaur gather at the tower. Hratha appears after them. Khan Hratha carries part of a key, and Warug wants you to bring it to him in Magram Village. He expects you to prove yourself an ally of the Magram.

quest:1398.text: Driftwood. Watcher Biggs sends you east to the coast for dry driftwood. He needs it to mend his wagon before he can reach Nethergarde. Watcher Biggs thanks you and asks for help again. His wagon needs repairs before he can reach Nethergarde. The swamp's wood is too spongy and tangled to use, so he needs strong, dry wood. Watcher Biggs sends you east to the coast for driftwood dried by the sun. Bring eight pieces back to him in the Swamp of Sorrows.

quest:1419.text: Coyote Thieves. In Kargath, crag coyotes have stolen food, and Neeka Bloodscar wants them hunted. She asks you to bring back thirty jawbones. Neeka Bloodscar asks whether you have spent many days in the Badlands, felt its heat, and met the beasts of its dusty plains. Crag coyotes are tough, and they have crept into Kargath to steal food from the outpost. She wants you to hunt them and bring back their jawbones. Bring enough, and Neeka may believe you know the Badlands.

quest:1420.text: Report to Helgrum. At Kargath, Neeka Bloodscar gives you a fresh report for Helgrum the Swift in Stonard. You have just spoken with her there. Neeka Bloodscar gives you a fresh report for Helgrum in Stonard. She warns that anyone who calls themselves an outrunner must keep the way and avoid falling to an enemy.

quest:1422.text: Threat From the Sea. Tok'Kar works on your weapon while Katar reports the beach patrols could use help. Tok'Kar works on your weapon and sends you to Katar. Katar says the beach patrols could use help. Some louses at camp drink, but Tok'Kar would rather you keep your wits sharp and your weapons ready than join them.

quest:1423.text: The Lost Supplies. A barrel bound for Nethergarde Keep bears Quartermaster Lungertz’s name. Pungent yellow wax seals the seams of a small, sturdy barrel. Its base carries a stamp naming Quartermaster Lungertz and Nethergarde Keep, marking where it belongs.

quest:1424.text: Pool of Tears. In Stonard, Fel'zerul sends you to search the Pool of Tears for Atal'ai artifacts. The Warchief's people came to investigate strange events at the Temple of Atal'Hakkar and found it sunk. The Atal'ai trolls are a tribe of dark casters known for forbidden magic. Fel'zerul's party reached the Temple of Atal'Hakkar and found it sunk. Green dragons now watch over the temple and call themselves protectors of Azeroth. Fel'zerul wants to learn what happened, so he asks you to gather Atal'ai artifacts around the Pool of Tears. The pieces may help the puzzle come together. No one knows what dark rites the trolls practiced in the temple, only that they used great magical forces. Fel'zerul hopes their spells may aid the Horde. He wants to learn what the Atal'ai sought and what went so horribly wrong.

quest:1425.text: Deliver the Shipment. After Driftwood, Watcher Biggs asks you to carry supplies to Quartermaster Lungertz at Nethergarde Keep while his wagon is repaired. Watcher Biggs packs the key supplies rescued from the ogre attacks for you to carry. He stays behind to repair the wagon. Nethergarde Keep lies in the Blasted Lands' northern hills and watches over the Dark Portal. Biggs sends you east along the road, then south into the Blasted Lands where it branches. At the next fork, take the left turn and stay wary.

quest:1426.text: Threat From the Sea. Tok'Kar sends you to Katar in the Swamp of Sorrows. Katar hates the sea and takes pleasure in seeing fish men fall to those who serve the Horde. Now Katar asks how many you can slay and whether you can face their strongest kind. In the Swamp of Sorrows, Katar asks you to kill marsh murlocs, marsh inkspewers and marsh flesheaters. Katar despises the sea and every creature from it. To Katar, the sea is a strong but blind, callous and brutal mistress. Slaying fish men by the hundreds would delight Katar, if that were possible. For now, watching them fall to those who serve the Horde brings some satisfaction.

quest:1427.text: Threat From the Sea. Katar sends you back to Tok'Kar before you rest. He believes Tok'Kar finished a few weapons while you were away, and one will be offered to you for your help. Before you rest, Katar sends you back to Tok'Kar. He believes Tok'Kar finished a few weapons while you were away. Tok'Kar will offer you one for your help. Katar says you could test its strength against the murlocs when ready, which would please him further.

quest:1428.text: Continued Threat. Along the Swamp of Sorrows beach, Katar sees your hatred of the fish men growing like her own. Katar sends you farther along the beach to hunt marsh inkspewers, marsh flesheaters and marsh oracles. Return when you have had enough of the fight. She will take no pleasure until the sea and all her children are silenced, with the repulsive fish men foremost in her thoughts.

quest:1429.text: The Atal'ai Exile. At Stonard, Fel'zerul sends you north with the artifacts from the Pool of Tears. Find an exiled Atal'ai priest in the Hinterlands and learn what the artifacts are for. A blood-marked scroll sentences an Atal'ai priest to a fate worse than death among his own people. He is sent to live with the Witherbark trolls, far north in the Hinterlands. Fel'zerul bundles the artifacts and sends you to find the exile, learn their true use, and return.

quest:1430.text: Fresh Meat. Dar needs crawler legs from the coast for hungry customers in Orgrimmar. Dar's customers in Orgrimmar crave crawler meat, especially from the monstrous crawlers. East of here, the creatures scurry over the beaches and into the surf. Bring back some of their legs, and Dar promises a cask of wine. He means to taste the meat before it goes on to Orgrimmar.

quest:1444.text:
Return to Fel'Zerul. In the Hinterlands, the Atal'ai Exile sends word to Fel'zerul in Stonard. The artifacts you brought are harmless, but the exile fears what Jammal'an the Prophet may do. The Atal'ai Exile once held Jammal'an the Prophet worthy of the high priesthood. Now the exile fears his unyielding faith in the prophecy may doom the Atal'ai, if it has not already. Speaking out earned the exile the name infidel and banishment from the Temple of Atal'Hakkar.

The artifacts you brought are harmless. Yet danger may lie in the summoning ritual, for Jammal'an may have found the right fetish enchantment. The world could be in great peril. Fel'zerul in Stonard waits to hear what the exile learned.

quest:1450.text: Gryphon Master Talonaxe. Inside the Aerie Peak Aviary, flight assignments fall to Gryphon Master Talonaxe. Falstad Wildhammer sends you there after turning away someone who came for an old Explorers' League friend. Falstad Wildhammer has little patience for a visitor sent by an old Explorers' League member. He does not know who that friend once flew with, and flight assignments belong to the gryphon master. You can find Gryphon Master Talonaxe inside the Aerie Peak Aviary. Falstad has real work for anyone who stays nearby.

quest:1451.text:
Rhapsody Shindigger. At the Aerie Peak Aviary, Talonaxe has news of a fallen flyer. Rhapsody Shindigger was once its finest flyer, but liquor cost Rhapsody the post. Now Rhapsody keeps a brewing camp east of the aviary, in the Hinterlands, Talonaxe has heard. Gryphon Master Talonaxe says the aviary dwarves all enjoy a good ale. Rhapsody took to liquor as readily as a gryphon takes to the skies. No one could fly like Rhapsody, and Talonaxe still regrets the loss.

The trouble began when Rhapsody returned stumbling from a trip with Brohann. Things worsened quickly, and the aviary let Rhapsody go. Talonaxe’s last word is that Rhapsody now keeps a brew camp east of Aerie Peak.

quest:1452.text: Rhapsody's Kalimdor Kocktail. In the Hinterlands, Rhapsody Shindigger is ready to tell you what happened in the swamp, once he has a stiff drink. His Kalimdor Kocktail needs Roc gizzards from Tanaris and Groddoc and Ironfur livers from Feralas. Rhapsody greets Brohann's messenger with a hiccup. The two shared quite an adventure, but Rhapsody will tell you what happened in the swamp only after a stiff drink. The tale is not pretty. He has a recipe in mind: the Kalimdor Kocktail. Once it is brewed, he promises to tell you everything. Rhapsody needs three Roc gizzards from Tanaris, three Groddoc livers from Feralas, and three Ironfur livers from Feralas. Even his finest malt cannot help him face the memory of that fateful flight over the swamp.

quest:1466.text: Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. In Desolace, Kreldig Ungor has the last items Leftwitch requested. They all come from demons: brains, wings, and blood. Kreldig Ungor warns you that the final set is grim and slower to gather than any before. Leftwitch wants ten of each of three kinds of parts. You can take felhound brains from mana eaters, mage hunters, or ley hunters. The wings come from nether maidens, sisters, or sorceresses, while doomwarder captains and lords carry the blood. Kreldig would understand if you passed on this one. Kreldig Ungor had not known these demons lived in Desolace. His reading said the centaur held most of the land after the night elves departed years ago. So he wonders how the demons came here and why they settled. They dwell near Mannoroc Coven in southern Desolace, beyond the Kodo Graveyard.

quest:1467.text: Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. In Desolace, Kreldig Ungor sends you to Ironforge with Leftwitch's package. Roetten Stonehammer has your pay, and Kreldig plans to speak well of you when he returns home. Kreldig says Roetten Stonehammer has your pay in Ironforge. Roetten will be glad to receive Leftwitch's package, and handing it over should be enough to collect what you are owed. Kreldig expects to stay in Desolace only a little longer. Once he is home, he still means to speak well of you.

quest:1469.text: Rhapsody's Tale. After Rhapsody Shindigger gets his Kalimdor Kocktail, he tells of the flight with Brohann Caskbelly. He gives you an Atal'ai Tablet Fragment to take to Brohann in Stormwind. Rhapsody Shindigger tells you what happened after the kocktail. Before the flight, he drank a whole keg of stout while Brohann followed him through the sky. Rhapsody kept a troll souvenir, an Atal'ai Tablet Fragment. Now he asks you to take it to Brohann Caskbelly in Stormwind.

quest:1488.text: The Corrupter. Takata Steelblade sides with Maurin: Lord Azrethoc must be stopped, especially if he seeks influence over the Burning Blade. Takata trusts you to gather a party against the demon lord and his warlock servant, Jugkar Grim'rod. Takata has never heard of Lord Azrethoc, but agrees with Maurin that the demon lord must be stopped. The danger grows if Azrethoc is trying to sway the Burning Blade. You have already shown that you want to aid the Warchief, so Takata trusts you to gather a party and slay Azrethoc and his warlock servant, Jugkar Grim'rod. Head directly south to Mannoroc Coven, where both are found. Takata calls the demons in Desolace a greater threat than ever. Each newly arrived foul creature dims the prospect of returning to the Warchief. At times, Takata wishes the centaur were the only enemy.

quest:1560.text: Tooga's Quest. In Tanaris, you and Tooga are trying to reach Torta. She waits just south of Steamwheedle Port. Tooga wanders near a crashed goblin zeppelin by Thistleshrub Valley, unsure of the way home. His wife, Torta, sent him to fetch dinner. A wrong turn left him lost, so he asks you to lead him back to her. Torta waits just south of Steamwheedle Port, across Tanaris from Tooga. Reaching her means walking nearly the whole width of the zone.

quest:162.text: Rise of the Silithid. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser sends you to Darnassus with a report for Gracina Spiritmight, a night elf scholar and historian. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser wants the report in the hands of someone who knows such matters. Gracina Spiritmight is a night elf scholar and historian. She has spent much time studying life forms unique to Azeroth's ecology. Fizzledowser hopes she can judge the danger and find a way to halt it. At Fizzledowser's last word, Gracina lives in the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus.

quest:1690.text: Wastewander Justice. In Tanaris, the Wastewander hold nearly every well, and Gadgetzan's water supply is at risk. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle sends you east of town to bring justice to the Wastewander Bandits and Thieves. Without access to the wells held by Wastewander nomads, Gadgetzan's water supply will soon run dry. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle wants you to bring down ten Wastewander Bandits and Thieves east of town. Then you are to report back at once. He has a taste for goblin-style justice.

quest:1691.text: More Wastewander Justice. East and southeast of Gadgetzan, Bilgewhizzle now targets Wastewander rogues, assassins, and shadow mages. With fewer nomads left, the company can more easily reclaim the water wells. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle says you have done well, but the company needs fewer nomads before it can reclaim the wells. Now you face their rogues, assassins, and shadow mages east and southeast of Gadgetzan. Bilgewhizzle calls them a nasty lot. He insists the wells rightfully belong to the company.

quest:1707.text: Water Pouch Bounty. In Gadgetzan, Spigot Operator Luglunket asks you to recover the Wastewander water pouches stolen by the nomads. Bring them back from anywhere in the desert, and the Gadgetzan Water Company offers an official care package for every five. Spigot Operator Luglunket wants you to bring back the Wastewander water pouches you find in the desert. The nomads stole Gadgetzan's water, so every pouch helps the town reclaim what is its own. For every five pouches returned, the Gadgetzan Water Company offers an official care package.

quest:1878.text: Water Pouch Bounty. In Gadgetzan, Spigot Operator Luglunket welcomes you back for five more Wastewander water pouches. A care package waits with your name on it. Luglunket welcomes you back and asks for five more Wastewander water pouches. A care package is already set aside with your name on it.

quest:193.text: Panther Mastery. At Nesingwary's Expedition, Sir S. J. Erlgadin sets one final trial for you. You have hunted panthers before, but the expedition's party has failed to find Bhag'thera. Bring back the predator's fang to prove your skill as a master of the hunt. At Nesingwary's Expedition, Sir S. J. Erlgadin sets one last test for you. Bhag'thera still prowls Stranglethorn Vale, beyond the expedition's party's reach. Track down the great panther and bring back its fang as proof of your skill.

quest:196.text: Raptor Mastery. In Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary sends you after Jungle Stalkers. Ten wary raptors stand between you and his finest hunt. Hemet Nesingwary sends you after Jungle Stalkers, a harder quarry than the raptors you hunted before. They are wary and hard to track or kill. Find and fell ten in the jungle, then return to camp. Hemet will give you a lead on his finest hunt yet.

quest:197.text: Raptor Mastery. In Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary sends you after the raptor that has eluded even him. After your trials against lesser beasts, you are to track Tethis and bring its talon back to Hemet. Hemet Nesingwary tells you of Tethis, a vicious raptor that has escaped every hunter, even the expedition leader. Ajeck Rouack gave the beast its name. Among Stranglethorn's raptors, Tethis is the greatest challenge for a hunter. Tethis roams north of the Gurubashi Arena. Bring Hemet a talon from the slain raptor, and he will recognize you as a master raptor slayer. No other big game hunter has achieved that feat.

quest:202.text: Colonel Kurzen. At the Rebel Camp, Lieutenant Doren sends you against Colonel Kurzen and his inner guard. Their defeat could secure the rebels' survival. Lieutenant Doren's defectors have reached the final struggle against their former commander. You have helped suppress Kurzen's elite specialists, but the rebels remain in danger while he holds his jungle redoubt. Doren sends you into the Stockpile cave, where Kurzen directs his forces beside his subchiefs and elites. Lieutenant Doren needs proof that Kurzen has fallen. He asks you to bring back the rogue colonel's head and defeat his elites and subchiefs. The cave confrontation gives the rebels their only chance to breathe easier amid the dangers of northern Stranglethorn.

quest:205.text: Troll Witchery. Brother Nimetz sends you into Skullsplitter territory to learn what has corrupted Colonel Kurzen. After Kurzen's Mystery, he asks you to gather fetishes from the tribe's spellcasters. Brother Nimetz suspects dark troll magic lies behind Colonel Kurzen's fall into evil. Legends recovered from the jungle have led him to the second troll tribe farther south. So he asks you to enter Skullsplitter lands and take fetishes from their Witch Doctors and Mystics. He will study the magic they carry at the Rebel Camp.

quest:206.text: Mai'Zoth. In the eastern mountains of Stranglethorn Vale, Mai'Zoth keeps a relic said to twist minds. Brother Nimetz believes the ogre mage corrupted Colonel Kurzen and wants the relic recovered before another commander suffers the same fate. Brother Nimetz believes the power behind Kurzen's rebellion remains. His research points to Mai'Zoth, an ogre mage who lives in an ogre mound in the eastern heights of Stranglethorn Vale. Nimetz says Mai'Zoth used sorcery to warp Kurzen's thoughts. While Mai'Zoth lives, another commander could suffer the same corruption. Brother Nimetz asks you to slay Mai'Zoth and take the Mind's Eye from him. Bring the artifact to the Rebel Camp.

quest:208.text:
Big Game Hunter. In Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary’s hunt for King Bangalash reaches its last trial. The famed marksman came to the jungle for the great white tiger. You have slain Sin'Dall, Bhag'thera, and Tethis in the trials set by the expedition's huntsmen. Hemet Nesingwary now knows your skill with weapons. Few have shown him finer skill on Lordaeron's battlefields or deep in the jungle.

One hunt remains. Bring down King Bangalash, the great white tiger Hemet came to hunt, and prove your abilities unmatched. King Bangalash drew Hemet Nesingwary to Stranglethorn Vale. The great beast has driven the expedition leader back to camp in defeat time and again. Its head would prove your hunting skill second to none.

quest:209.text: Skullsplitter Tusks. In Booty Bay, Kebok struggles to fill orders for tiger fangs bound for the South Seas. Real fangs cost too much to supply, so he has found another way to meet demand. Kebok’s trade in tiger fangs for buyers across the South Seas has grown costly and hard to supply through ordinary hunting. So he has found a way to shape horn-like objects into convincing fangs without leaving a sign of the trick. Skullsplitter troll tusks make the closest match. Kebok hires adventurers to take eighteen from the jungle tribe for his next shipment.

quest:243.text: Into the Field. In Tanaris, you test desert creatures with Apothecary Zinge’s field testing kit. Its power source must come from Gadgetzan’s goblins, so Zinge sends you to Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle. Apothecary Zinge needs to know whether tissue from Tanaris basilisks, scorpids and hyenas is consistent. You gather samples and test them with the field testing kit. Many will fail, so Zinge needs eight acceptable samples of each kind. Return only when you have them. The modified kit needs a power source like those held by Gadgetzan’s goblins. Zinge sends you to Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan to get one.

quest:2605.text: The Thirsty Goblin. In Gadgetzan, Marin Noggenfogger longs for a drink that can end his unending thirst. He has heard the dew collectors in the cactus garden southwest of town keep water in special glands, and hopes one will make such a drink possible. Marin Noggenfogger has heard of dew collectors in the cactus garden southwest of Gadgetzan. They keep water in special glands, and he believes a full gland could start a drink that ends his thirst for good. He asks you to find their garden and bring one back.

quest:2606.text: In Good Taste. Marin Noggenfogger finds thistleshrub dew awful to drink, yet he keeps working on the brew. He sends you to Sprinkle in Gadgetzan with the dew. Marin Noggenfogger tastes the dew and finds it awful. Still, he keeps working on the drink. He sends you to Sprinkle, his friend in Gadgetzan and an excellent chef. You carry the dew and explain that the drink needs to go down more easily. Marin also wants it to have some kick.

quest:2622.text: The Missing Orders. Dispatch Commander Ruag sends you to find Bengor after the orders go missing. Dispatch Commander Ruag bristles when you ask about the missing orders. He says they went with the soldiers sent to carry them. Murlocs ambushed and brutally beat the soldiers, and only one survived. Bengor can barely speak, cannot walk, and is fed through a tube. Ruag sends you to find him nearby, then warns you to mind what you poke your nose into.

quest:2623.text: The Swamp Talker. Orders bound for the Blasted Lands vanish in a murloc ambush. Bengor tells you what happened before he loses consciousness. Bengor says the dispatch commander gave out the orders. His group was bound for the Blasted Lands when many murlocs fell upon them. One of them, Swamp Talker, seized the orders from Bengor as a spear struck his skull. Before he passes out, Bengor speaks of a cave to the east. Recover the orders and take them to the Fallen Hero of the Horde.

quest:2641.text: Sprinkle's Secret Ingredient. In Gadgetzan, Sprinkle offers a way to make Marin Noggenfogger's foul brew drinkable with a Violet Tragan. The mushroom grows underwater in a small lake in the Hinterlands. As a child, Sprinkle's sister did all the cooking, and the food was hard to stomach. Sprinkle found a mushroom called the Violet Tragan and made it her secret ingredient. She says it made every dish taste wonderful. Now she will use it to make Marin's horrid brew drinkable. The Violet Tragan grows underwater in a small lake in the Hinterlands. Valorwind Lake lies just south of the road that crosses the zone. Dive beneath the surface to gather the mushroom, then return to Sprinkle in Gadgetzan.

quest:2661.text: Delivery for Marin. In Gadgetzan, Sprinkle sends Violet Powder to Marin Noggenfogger and reminds her of the favor Marin owes. In Gadgetzan, Sprinkle gives you Violet Powder after you bring her the Violet Tragan. Marin Noggenfogger is in the same town, and Sprinkle asks you to remind Marin that she owes a favor.

quest:2662.text: Noggenfogger Elixir. In Gadgetzan, Marin Noggenfogger works Violet Powder into the dew. He asks you to return in a moment, when his fabulous elixir should be ready. Marin has the dew and the powder. He begins mixing them, and the Noggenfogger Elixir should be ready after a short wait. Then speak to him again.

quest:2741.text: The Super Egg-O-Matic. At the control panel, Curgle Cranklehop's newest invention sputters wildly as hippogryph eggs go into the machine. At its control panel, Curgle Cranklehop's newest invention sputters wildly. It takes a hippogryph egg found in the mountains of southern Feralas, around the Ruins of Isildien.

quest:2742.text: Rin'ji is Trapped!. At Quel'Danil Lodge, Rin'ji has lost an axe and is held captive. Rin'ji asks a passer-by for help escaping, offers something in return, and speaks of a secret at the Overlook Cliffs. At Quel'Danil Lodge, Rin'ji is frightened and held captive. The axe is gone, so Rin'ji begs a passer-by to help escape. Many dislike Rin'ji's kind. Still, Rin'ji offers something to a kind soul who helps and says a secret lies hidden at the Overlook Cliffs.

quest:2747.text: An Extraordinary Egg. In Tanaris, Curgle Cranklehop seeks an extraordinary egg from Feralas. Curgle Cranklehop says few eggs from Feralas arrive in extraordinary shape. Such eggs are the rarest of all. One is what Curgle seeks.

quest:2748.text: A Fine Egg. Curgle Cranklehop speaks of an egg that may hatch free of the Gordunni ogres’ evil incantations. Curgle Cranklehop says an egg has a good chance of hatching untouched by the Gordunni ogres’ wicked chanting, if conditions are ideal.

quest:2749.text: An Ordinary Egg. Curgle Cranklehop tends ordinary hippogryph eggs, though only about half hatch. Only about half of ordinary hippogryph eggs hatch. Curgle Cranklehop does their best to nurture each one, hoping luck will see it hatch.

quest:2750.text: A Bad Egg. Curgle Cranklehop takes charge when a hippogryph egg cannot be saved. Some hippogryph eggs cannot be saved. Curgle Cranklehop handles those that will never hatch.

quest:2766.text: Find OOX-22/FE!. A homing robot has crashed in Feralas, and Oglethorpe Obnoticus calls for help through a strange metal egg. Carry its beacon to a cave near Feral Scar Vale. Turn the knob on the metal egg, and it opens into a gnomish contraption. Oglethorpe Obnoticus speaks from within. His homing robot has crashed, and he promises payment if you recover it. He has worked out that the machine lies in a cave near Feral Scar Vale. Carry the beacon there.

quest:2767.text: Rescue OOX-22/FE!. In Feral Scar Vale, OOX-22/FE! waits for your help on the way to the Forgotten Coast dock. Once it arrives, Oglethorpe Obnoticus wants to speak with you in Booty Bay. OOX-22/FE needs an open, safe place for its lengthy take-off. The gnome's voice crackles through the robot as he explains that its built-in cloaking needs time before it works again. Oglethorpe Obnoticus also needs time to make it work. He suggests the Forgotten Coast dock, where everything can be brought online. You escort the robot there from where it stands. Once OOX-22/FE reaches the dock safely, Oglethorpe Obnoticus wants you to speak with him in Booty Bay.

quest:2781.text: WANTED: Caliph Scorpidsting. Across Gadgetzan and Steamwheedle Port, notices call for Caliph Scorpidsting, leader of the Wastewander outlaws. The Gadgetzan Water Company seeks proof of his death in Gadgetzan. In Gadgetzan and Steamwheedle Port, the Gadgetzan Water Company posts a high bounty for Caliph Scorpidsting. The notices accuse him of murdering company employees, stealing its resources and seizing its property. Bring proof of his death to Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan.

quest:2782.text: Rin'ji's Secret. After helping Rin'ji, you carry Rin'ji's Secret, a tablet marked in Witherbark script that no one has read. Oran Snakewrithe studies the Witherbark and may decipher it. He is known to live in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Witherbark troll markings cover the tablet, but what Rin'ji's secret is remains a mystery. It may be worth a great deal or nothing at all. A Witherbark troll in trouble might try anything to escape it. Oran Snakewrithe is a well-known scholar of the Witherbark trolls. He is known to live in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity and may be able to read the tablet.

quest:2821.text: The Mark of Quality. At Feathermoon Stronghold, Pratt McGrubben seeks ten thick yeti hides and offers a choice of leather goods. Pratt McGrubben, a leatherworker at Feathermoon Stronghold, insists on the finest work. In search of fine materials, he found thick yeti hides. Yetis are native to Feralas, and many live around Feral Scar Vale, just inland of the Forgotten Coast. Bring Pratt a stack of ten hides at Feathermoon Stronghold. In return, you may choose one of the leather goods he has crafted.

quest:2822.text: The Mark of Quality. At Camp Mojache, Jangdor Swiftstrider seeks ten thick yeti hides and will not compromise on quality. Jangdor Swiftstrider takes pride in fine leatherwork. He has found thick yeti hides in Feralas, where the yetis make their home. Many roam west of Camp Mojache in Feral Scar Vale, just inland of the Forgotten Coast. Bring Jangdor a stack of ten hides at Camp Mojache. In return, he will let you choose one of the leather goods he has made.

quest:2844.text: The Giant Guardian. Rockbiter searches for Shay, the night elf girl he was meant to watch over. Worried, he asks you to look for her. Rockbiter last saw Shay while they walked through the ruins just north of where he stands. Then he turned around, and she was gone. Unsure what to do, he asks you to search for his little friend. Your legs can carry you much faster than his.

quest:2845.text: Wandering Shay. Shay Leafrunner is distracted by the sights along the way as she tries to return to Rockbiter, her friend. Shay was meant to be watched by Rockbiter. She wants to return to him, but the many things around her catch her eye and lead her astray. A bell in the chest beside Shay always catches her attention, and she treasures its sound. If she wanders off, ring it and she promises to come running back. You can carry the bell to Rockbiter's camp, where Shay hopes to be taken.

quest:2862.text: War on the Woodpaw. At Camp Mojache, Hadoken Swiftstrider asks you to thin the Woodpaw gnolls’ growing numbers. Their attacks have grown more fevered, and ten Woodpaw Gnoll Manes will answer his call. Hadoken Swiftstrider says the camp’s survival matters more than the gnolls’ claim to Feralas. Unless Camp Mojache stands firm, he warns, the gnolls may drive it from the whole region. Their attacks have grown more fevered, so he wants their numbers thinned. For ten Woodpaw gnoll manes, he offers generous pay.

quest:2863.text: Alpha Strike. The Horde's stalemate with the Woodpaw gnolls may be broken by striking their leaders in quick succession. Hadoken Swiftstrider asks you to bring down five Alphas within one hour. Hadoken Swiftstrider believes the Woodpaw ranks will fall into chaos if their Alphas die one after another. The blows may also show the gnolls that the Horde can destroy them. He asks you to carry out the plan. Five Alphas must fall within one hour, or the stalemate continues.

quest:2866.text: The Ruins of Solarsal. South of Shandris Feathermoon, Hatecrest naga crowd the Ruins of Solarsal. She sends you among the old stones to look for anything out of the ordinary. Shandris Feathermoon says explorers searched the ruins long ago and found nothing of note. So the stones were left alone. Now Hatecrest naga have taken them in alarming numbers. Their presence first seemed to herald an attack, and that danger remains. Yet Shandris suspects something else may be happening. She asks you to walk through the ruins and notice anything out of the ordinary.

quest:2867.text: Return to Feathermoon Stronghold. You return to Feathermoon Stronghold with news of a strange gazebo at the heart of the Ruins of Solarsal. General Shandris Feathermoon awaits your report. At Feathermoon Stronghold, General Shandris Feathermoon awaits your news of the strange gazebo. You carry your findings back from the heart of the ruins so she can hear what you saw.

quest:2869.text: Against the Hatecrest. At Feathermoon Stronghold, Latronicus Moonspear means to face the Hatecrest naga before they make their move. He asks you to bring him ten Hatecrest Scales in good condition. Latronicus Moonspear expects the naga to try to claim the island someday. He wants to act before they can, so he asks you to bring ten Hatecrest Scales in good condition. You will have to see for yourself how to get them. He hopes gathering the scales will weaken the naga presence on Sardor Isle and give you your first taste of fighting naga. Latronicus says night elves cherish peace and harmony, not war. Still, he will not leave their interests unguarded. Protecting them is his duty to General Feathermoon and the stronghold.

quest:2870.text: Against Lord Shalzaru. At Feathermoon Stronghold, Latronicus Moonspear asks you to stop Lord Shalzaru and recover the relic he found. Latronicus Moonspear has fresh reports on the naga chain of command. Royals give orders among their ranks. Lord Shalzaru is one of the crueler royals. Scouts say Lord Shalzaru uncovered an odd relic while the naga dug in a cave on the Isle of Dread. The cave lies over the water, south of the main ruins. Latronicus wants you to stop Shalzaru and end the dig. Then bring the Mysterious Relic to Feathermoon Stronghold for study.

quest:2871.text: Delivering the Relic. At Feathermoon Stronghold, Latronicus Moonspear sends you with the Mysterious Relic to his wife Vestia. He cannot make sense of it, and hopes she can tell what it is. Latronicus Moonspear cannot make sense of the device, wager or no wager. He says his wife Vestia is a fine priestess to their community and one of the most learned scholars anywhere. If anyone can work out what the relic is, she can. They need to know. Vestia is only a short walk away, though she is surely busy studying.

quest:2872.text:
Stoley's Debt. At Steamwheedle Port, “Sea Wolf” MacKinley wants the rum Stoley wagered with him. He asks you to speak with the barkeep about it. “Sea Wolf” MacKinley says Stoley owes him a special bottle of rum. Stoley boasted that Steamwheedle Port’s rum was stronger than anything in Booty Bay. He promised to double the money he owes MacKinley if MacKinley tried it and disagreed.

Now MacKinley thinks Stoley has lost his nerve about handing over the bottle. But MacKinley never backs away from a wager, so he asks you to speak with Stoley at the Steamwheedle Port bar.

quest:2873.text: Stoley's Shipment. Stoley is out of rum and asks you to recover his stolen shipment. Captain Cuergo keeps it in Lost Rigger Cove, the walled pirate town to the south. Stoley owes “Sea Wolf” MacKinley of Booty Bay rum for their wager, but his supply is gone. Captain Cuergo took the last shipment and keeps it in Lost Rigger Cove, the walled pirate town to the south. Stoley wants you to bring the rum back so he can prove Kalimdor’s drink is better than anything Booty Bay pours. The pirates keep the rum in crates on the upper floor of the house in the northwest.

quest:2874.text: Deliver to MacKinley. At Steamwheedle Port, Stoley gives you bilge rum for MacKinley in Booty Bay. The Sea Wolf can judge whether the drink settles his beliefs about Booty Bay booze. After you help with the shipment, Stoley gives you a bottle of Steamwheedle bilge rum. You carry it to MacKinley in Booty Bay, where he can finally set aside his beliefs about the booze there.

quest:2875.text: WANTED: Andre Firebeard. In Gadgetzan and Steamwheedle Port, a wanted notice names Andre Firebeard and accuses him of crimes against both places. Deliver his head to Security Chief Bilgewhizzle at Steamwheedle Port, and it counts as a binding contract. A notice condemns Andre Firebeard as a vile pirate accused of crimes against Steamwheedle and Gadgetzan. The governing counsel allows anyone who reads it to use lethal force to capture Andre and those who aid him. He can be found at the pirate enclave south along the coast from Steamwheedle Port, standing by a campfire inside its walls. A further decree says Andre's head may speak for him if he is dead or otherwise unable to attend his hearing. Delivered to Security Chief Bilgewhizzle at Steamwheedle Port, it counts as a binding contract.

quest:2876.text: Ship Schedules. At Steamwheedle Port, some voyages bear marks on the ship schedule. It belongs with someone in authority there. Ships sail between Steamwheedle Port and Booty Bay, and the scroll names them all. It records voyages already made and those still to come. Large X marks cross some journeys. Notes beside others warn of plunder or a hard fight. Someone in authority at Steamwheedle Port needs the schedule.

quest:2877.text: Skulk Rock Clean-up. Sludges and oozes overrun the Horde's old positions around Skulk Rock. Fraggar Thundermantle at Aerie Peak wants them cleared, for the Wildhammers have plans for the ground. The Wildhammers remember the past more than their brothers in Ironforge do. Fraggar Thundermantle says friends are made here by getting your hands dirty. The Horde left its positions around Skulk Rock in the Hinterlands, and sludges and oozes have overrun them. The Wildhammers have plans for that ground, but first the infestation must be thinned. Slay ten green sludges and ten jade oozes. Then return to Fraggar at Aerie Peak with your report.

quest:2879.text: The Stave of Equinex. At the Ruins of Ravenwind, Troyas Moonbreeze tests whether his stave can open the Equinex Monolith. You gather the essences of four flames still burning among the ruins. Troyas Moonbreeze thinks his stave may be the Stave of Equinex, a key to the Equinex Monolith in the Ruins of Ravenwind. Four flames still burn there: Samha, Imbel, Byltan and Lahassa. Each yields an essence. You use all four at the monolith to energize the stave. If it is truly the key, the monolith will open and reveal a sacred artifact.

quest:2880.text: Troll Necklace Bounty. At Aerie Peak, Fraggar Thundermantle asks you to bring him five necklaces from trolls in the Hinterlands. Fraggar Thundermantle trusts deeds over words. The Wildhammers answer to no Alliance, and anyone seeking their friendship must prove their worth first. Trolls roaming the Hinterlands hillsides sometimes wear tribal necklaces. Bring five to Fraggar at Aerie Peak, and you will have made a start.

quest:2881.text: Troll Necklace Bounty. For Fraggar Thundermantle, troll tribal necklaces still come in batches of five. The Wildhammer has already accepted one batch from you, and the offer remains open. Fraggar Thundermantle welcomes more troll tribal necklaces whenever you find them and choose to hand them over. He says the Wildhammers will fight for those who fight for them. Each batch must hold five necklaces.

quest:2902.text: Woodpaw Investigation. At Camp Mojache, Hadoken Swiftstrider suspects the Woodpaw gnolls are following written plans. He sends you south to search their camps for battle plans. After Alpha Strike, Hadoken Swiftstrider sends you back to the Woodpaw. He doubts the gnolls are clever, yet their recent assaults have been too well coordinated to be chance. He suspects they keep a written record of their strategy. If you find it, he may learn what stirred them up, so he asks you to search the camps and bring back anything that looks like battle plans.

quest:2903.text: The Battle Plans. You carry the Woodpaw battle plans toward Camp Mojache, where Hadoken Swiftstrider hopes to learn what the gnolls intend. After Woodpaw Investigation, you bring the Woodpaw battle plans back to Hadoken Swiftstrider at Camp Mojache. He needs firm evidence of what the gnolls intend.

quest:2932.text: Grim Message. In Stranglethorn, Nimboya sends you north to punish the Witherbark trolls for betraying Thrall. He gives you a pike to bear their skulls and plant in one of their Hinterlands villages. Nimboya sends you from Stranglethorn to the Hinterlands, far to the north and northeast of Tarren Mill, a village held by the Forsaken. The Witherbark trolls once stood with the Horde, but betrayed Thrall. Hunt them for their skulls, then plant Nimboya's pike in Hiri'watha or Zun'watha, two of their smaller villages. The warning will show them what their deeds cost. Nimboya waits in Stranglethorn.

quest:2933.text: Venom Bottles. In the Hinterlands, Venom Bottles fill a Witherbark village. Their great number suggests the Witherbarks value the vile green venom, and an apothecary in nearby Tarren Mill may want a sample. Vile green venom fills bottles throughout the Witherbark village. There are many of them, suggesting the Witherbarks consider the venom important. An apothecary in Tarren Mill may want a sample to examine.

quest:2934.text: Undamaged Venom Sac. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon needs a fresh sample of venom. You search the Hinterlands for the spiders that yield it, and the sac must reach him fresh. After Venom Bottles, Apothecary Lydon asks you for a fresher sample. The spiders that yield the venom live in the Hinterlands, many near the troll city of Shadra'Alor. Lydon wants an undamaged venom sac, delivered while it is fresh. He is eager to experiment with it and has ordered several small, terribly cute animals for testing.

quest:2935.text:
Consult Master Gadrin. In Sen'jin Village, Apothecary Lydon seeks a stronger venom sample. The broodguard venom you brought was weaker than your first sample, so another kind of spider may be the source. Apothecary Lydon needs a fresh sample of the stronger venom. The broodguard venom you brought was weaker than your first sample, so it must come from another kind of spider.

Lydon sends you to Master Gadrin in Sen'jin Village, in Durotar. Gadrin is a troll well acquainted with the Witherbark, and may know where the venom comes from.

quest:2937.text: Summoning Shadra. At Shadra'Alor, you read Master Gadrin's parchment and call Shadra from the Witherbark realm. Master Gadrin sends you deep into the Witherbark realm of the Hinterlands. At Shadra'Alor, you read his parchment at the altar, and Shadra the spider god answers. Defeat her there, then carry her venom to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill.

quest:2938.text: Venom to the Undercity. Apothecary Lydon sends spider god venom to the Undercity. Its strength delights Lydon, who entrusts you with a parcel for Faranell, a superior at the Apothecarium. Apothecary Lydon has killed nearly two dozen rabbits with one dose of the venom. Some were tiny, so their resistance was surely low. Even so, the poison is powerful. Lydon is certain Faranell will want to test it personally, and gives you a parcel for the Apothecarium in the Undercity.

quest:2939.text: In Search of Knowledge. Troyas Moonbreeze sends you to seek Daryn Lightwind in Rut'theran Village. He found a stave in the rubble of Feralas and wants to learn what it is. Troyas Moonbreeze says the ruins of Feralas are dangerous, yet they have much to tell of what happened there. A few days ago, he searched the rubble to the south and found a stave that seemed ordinary. Still, he feels there is more to it. He and Angelas searched their books, but found no word of the stave. Troyas has a colleague in Darnassus who may know what the stave is. He asks you to speak with Daryn Lightwind in Rut'theran Village.

quest:2940.text: Feralas: A History. In Feralas, you find Feralas: A History, a book Troyas may need. It looks as if nobody has opened it in ages. The book belongs to Daryn Lightwind, so you need to ask whether you may borrow it. The book's covers are badly worn, and its pages have yellowed. After looking it over, you suspect it may be what Troyas is searching for. You pick it up, then think better of borrowing it without asking. It belongs to Daryn Lightwind, so ask her first.

quest:2941.text: The Borrower. On the Hinterlands beach, Daryn Lightwind longs to see Gammerita, a giant snapjaw. Her research keeps her away, so she sends you to Tanaris with a letter for Curgle Cranklehop. Daryn Lightwind has studied many subjects. Now the snapjaws along the Hinterlands beach hold her attention, especially Gammerita, a giant snapjaw. Her research keeps her where she is, so she asks you to bring back a picture of Gammerita. Daryn gives you a letter for Curgle Cranklehop in Tanaris. Curgle made an invention that can capture a picture. Daryn believes Curgle calls it a snapshot.

quest:2942.text: The Morrow Stone. At the Equinex Monolith, taking the artifact begins to drain the Stave of Equinex. You carry the Sparkling Stone and the stave back to Troyas Moonbreeze at Feathermoon Stronghold. The Stave of Equinex begins to lose energy when you take the artifact from the monolith. Troyas Moonbreeze at Feathermoon Stronghold awaits word of what you found. Bring him the Sparkling Stone and the stave.

quest:2943.text: Return to Troyas. Daryn Lightwind sends you to Feathermoon Stronghold with her book, Feralas: A History. Troyas Moonbreeze is eager for your return. After the Super Snapper FX, Daryn Lightwind entrusts you with her book, Feralas: A History. She urges you to hurry because Troyas Moonbreeze is eager for your return. The book is bound for Troyas at Feathermoon Stronghold.

quest:2944.text: The Super Snapper FX. Curgle Cranklehop has a new device for you to try: the Super Snapper FX. Aim it at Gammerita, a creature from the Hinterlands, then bring the picture and device to Daryn Lightwind in Rut'theran Village. This follows The Borrower. After The Borrower, Curgle Cranklehop puts a new invention in your hands: the Super Snapper FX. Aim it at what you want pictured, then press the button. Curgle gives it to you to try. Gammerita, a creature from the Hinterlands, is the subject you mentioned to Curgle. He wishes you luck in finding her and expects Daryn Lightwind to be pleased with the snapshot. Once you have the picture, bring it and the device to Daryn in Rut'theran Village.

quest:2954.text: The Stone Watcher. At the Uldum Pedestal, The Stone Watcher guards the way into the compound. You have carried the platinum discs across Tanaris, and now it asks you to learn its story before you go on. At the Uldum Pedestal, the Stone Watcher blocks the way into the Uldum compound. You brought the platinum discs across Tanaris. The guardian says entry is allowed only when the Plates of Uldum are part of your set. Learn the Watcher's story, then use the pedestal.

quest:2969.text: Freedom for All Creatures. At the Grimtotem camp, Kindal Moonweaver asks you to free the captured faerie dragons. Neither Kindal nor Jer'kai knows what the Grimtotem clan intends. Kindal will go with you, while Jer'kai stays behind. Kindal Moonweaver calls the Grimtotem clan filthy for taking faerie dragons. Neither Kindal nor Jer'kai knows what the clan intends, only that it means no good. They are not strong enough to fight into the camp, so Kindal asks you to help free the sprite darters. The Bamboo Cage Key opens their pen, and Kindal wants them to escape alive. Bring strong friends to stand with you. Kindal waits on a ledge behind the Grimtotem Compound, above the water. A path climbs the cliff face to reach him. Kindal fights beside you through the camp. Jer'kai stays behind.

quest:2970.text:
Doling Justice. In Feralas, Jer'kai Moonweaver and Kindal are ready to strike back after the sprite darters' rescue. Jer'kai asks you to thin the Grimtotem ranks, then return to him. After the sprite darter rescue, Jer'kai Moonweaver and Kindal are ready to strike at the Grimtotem. They can thin the tauren ranks together without much risk, and welcome your help.

You have seen the camp below, and more lie to the east. Choose your own tactics against Grimtotem Naturalists, Raiders and Shamans, then return to Jer'kai.

quest:2972.text: Doling Justice. In Feralas, Jer'kai Moonweaver sends you to Darnassus with a ring for High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. It will show that Jer'kai and Kindal are well and support your account. Jer'kai Moonweaver and Kindal have little to offer in Feralas, yet they want you to know they are grateful. Jer'kai gives you a signet ring for High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind at the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. The ring shows Tyrande that the pair are well and lends weight to your account.

quest:2973.text: A New Cloak's Sheen. At Camp Mojache, Krueg Skullsplitter asks you to gather wings for Korrin’s cloak. He came to Feralas with companions sent by their masters in Orgrimmar. Krueg Skullsplitter came to Feralas with companions sent by their masters in Orgrimmar. His life-mate Korrin loves new clothes, so he plans a cloak adorned with delicate faerie dragon wings. The sprite darters he seeks live west of Camp Mojache. Bring Krueg ten Iridescent Sprite Darter Wings. Krueg warns that provoked sprite darters are dangerous. Nearby night elves tend to hole up in the forests, so take even greater care around them.

quest:2974.text: A Grim Discovery. In Camp Mojache, Krueg Skullsplitter hears that you met tauren in Feralas and names them the Grimtotem. Belgrom has put a bounty on them, and Krueg asks for twenty horns. You tell Krueg Skullsplitter about the tauren you met in Feralas. He names them as the Grimtotem clan. Belgrom, one of Krueg's masters, has put a bounty on them and takes a keen interest in their kind. Krueg warns you that the Grimtotem are evil and must not be underestimated. He wants twenty horns brought back before they can raze villages or pilfer land.

quest:2975.text: The Ogres of Feralas. At Camp Mojache, Rok Orhan calls for the Gordunni to be driven back. Their outpost lies up the river to the north. Rok Orhan says the Gordunni ogres scar the land around Camp Mojache. Drive the tribe back before it reaches deeper into Feralas. Follow the river north to find their outpost. There, slay ten Gordunni Ogres, ten Gordunni Ogre-Magi and five Gordunni Brutes to show the tribe they are unwelcome.

quest:2976.text: A Grim Discovery. In Orgrimmar, Belgrom Rockmaul awaits the Grimtotem horns and your account of Feralas. Krueg Skullsplitter says you did the work and deserve the best of the bounty. This follows the first A Grim Discovery. Krueg Skullsplitter admits he spoke of a bounty after the first A Grim Discovery. You did the work, so he believes you deserve the best of the payoff. He packs the horns into a crate for you to carry to Belgrom Rockmaul in the Valley of Honor. Belgrom wants to hear what you saw, and Krueg says he will make your hard work worth it.

quest:2978.text: The Gordunni Scroll. At the Gordunni Outpost, the Gordunni Scroll may reveal a gathering or ceremony. Rok Orhan at Camp Mojache wants to see it and learn what it means for the Gordunni. You find a soiled scroll at the Gordunni Outpost. Its image seems to show a gathering or ceremony. Rok Orhan at Camp Mojache wants to see it and learn what it might mean for the Gordunni.

quest:2979.text: Dark Ceremony. At Camp Mojache, Rok Orhan studies the Gordunni Scroll and seeks an orb from a Gordunni mage-lord. He hopes it will reveal more about the ceremony and the Gordunni's magic. Rok Orhan reads the Gordunni Scroll as plans for a dark ceremony. He believes the Gordunni mage-lords conduct it. Find one of them and take his orb. A mage's orb holds great power, and Rok hopes it will teach him more about the ceremony and the magic the Gordunni wield.

quest:2980.text:
The Ogres of Feralas. In Feralas, Rok Orhan sends you southwest of Camp Mojache to drive back the Gordunni ogres. You have proved yourself a true fighter, and he trusts you with this work in the High Wilderness. Rok Orhan trusts you with this work because you have proved yourself a true fighter. Southwest of Camp Mojache, the High Wilderness holds abandoned, wrecked structures on ground the night elves once owned.

Withered trees and desecrated ground mark the Gordunni's territory. Rok warns that these ogres are far tougher than the earlier ones. Ten Gordunni Shamans, ten Gordunni Warlocks and five Gordunni Maulers are to fall.

quest:2982.text: The High Wilderness. In Feralas, Angelas Moonbreeze worries as Troyas enters the High Wilderness alone. Gordunni ogres hold that ground, and she hopes you can make the ruins southeast of here safer by culling them. Angelas Moonbreeze and Troyas explore the scattered ruins of Feralas, though the work is dangerous. Lately, Troyas goes to the High Wilderness alone, and Angelas fears for him. Gordunni ogres hold that ground and welcome no one into their territory. So Angelas asks you to make the ruins southeast of here safer for Troyas by culling eight Gordunni Warlocks, eight Gordunni Shamans and eight Gordunni Brutes.

quest:2987.text:
Gordunni Cobalt. Orwin Gizzmick has come to Feralas seeking cobalt buried by the Gordunni ogres. He asks you to search the Gordunni Outpost, north of Camp Mojache, for twelve samples. New to Feralas, Orwin Gizzmick has heard that the Gordunni ogres bury interesting minerals. They guard the minerals fiercely, keeping them from folk like Orwin. He does not know what they want them for.

Orwin gives you a shovel and points you north of Camp Mojache to the Gordunni Outpost. Follow the blue glow and dig up twelve samples of Gordunni cobalt.

quest:2988.text: Witherbark Cages. At Witherbark Cages, you search for Sharpbeak, heir of Swiftwing, whom Talonaxe calls the mightiest gryphon. Gryphon Master Talonaxe believes the trolls took the young gryphon. Gryphon Master Talonaxe asks you to find Sharpbeak, who went missing a few days ago while hunting with his parents. Talonaxe and the others believe the trolls took him. Three cages in the two Witherbark troll villages remain to be checked. Talonaxe awaits your findings.

quest:2989.text: The Altar of Zul. At the Altar of Zul, Talonaxe's search for Sharpbeak reaches the Vilebranch lands. Witherbark has no sign of the young gryphon, and Talonaxe fears the Vilebranch may hold him. With no sign of Sharpbeak in the Witherbark cages, Gryphon Master Talonaxe suspects the Vilebranch trolls took him. So he sends you to search the top of the Altar of Zul, at the western edge of their lands. If they hold the gryphon child, Talonaxe fears what they may be doing to him.

quest:2990.text: Thadius Grimshade. At Nethergarde Keep, Talonaxe sends you to Thadius Grimshade with a feather from Sharpbeak's nest. Years ago, Thadius Grimshade left Aerie Peak to seek darker knowledge. Yet Talonaxe says he remains a Wildhammer at heart. He hopes Thadius can use divining magic and Sharpbeak's feather to find the gryphon child. Thadius lives in the mage tower at Nethergarde Keep, in the Blasted Lands.

quest:2992.text: The Divination. Thadius Grimshade turns to Sharpbeak’s feather, seeking the gryphon through its trace. He asks you to give him room as he follows the bond to its owner. Thadius Grimshade follows the bond between Sharpbeak’s feather and the gryphon who owns it. He hopes to reach Sharpbeak himself, and asks you for silence and room to work. The ritual may not go as planned. If it does not, he warns, you had better close your eyes.

quest:2993.text: Return to the Hinterlands. You carry Thadius Grimshade's news of Sharpbeak to Gryphon Master Talonaxe. Thadius Grimshade has learned where Sharpbeak is held. The gryphon is caged on a high cliff atop Jintha'Alor in the Hinterlands. Vile Priestess Hexx, high priestess of the Vilebranch trolls, holds the key. You bring the news to Gryphon Master Talonaxe.

quest:2994.text: Saving Sharpbeak. At Jintha'Alor, Sharpbeak waits in a cage deep in Vilebranch territory. Gryphon Master Talonaxe sends you to free him, and Vile Priestess Hexx holds the key. After Thadius Grimshade's divination, you report to Talonaxe. Now the path to Sharpbeak is clear. Jintha'Alor lies at the heart of Vilebranch territory, and you fight your way to its summit. Vile Priestess Hexx holds the key to Sharpbeak's cage. Take it from her, then find the cage and free the gryphon.

quest:3002.text: The Gordunni Orb. After Dark Ceremony, Rok Orhan sends you to Orgrimmar with the Gordunni Orb. Uthel'nay at Darkbriar Lodge can judge its power. After Dark Ceremony, Rok Orhan holds the Gordunni Orb. He knows the Gordunni well, but a warrior cannot judge the orb's power. So he sends you to Orgrimmar with it. There, Uthel'nay at Darkbriar Lodge can tell you more.

quest:3022.text: Handle With Care. Curgle Cranklehop sends a crate of eggs to a druid in Rut'theran. The village lies in Teldrassil. Curgle Cranklehop entrusts you with a carefully packed crate for Erelas Ambersky. Hippogryph eggs lie inside, bound for the druid. Erelas Ambersky cares for hippogryph eggs in Rut'theran Village. He helps them hatch and trains the young hippogryphs. Rut'theran is a small village in southern Teldrassil.

quest:3062.text: Dark Heart. At Camp Mojache, Talo Thornhoof seeks Edana Hatetalon’s heart to end the hatred she spreads. Edana Hatetalon rules the Northspring brood in ruins to the west. Talo calls her pure evil and says she feels nothing but hatred for everyone. He has heard her heart is made of crystal. He asks you to face her and bring back her dark heart, so her hatred can be stopped. Talo has heard that harpies carry a horn. Sound it near the Hatetalon stones in the northern part of the ruins, and it is said to draw Edana out. Talo relishes the thought that death, rather than her kin, will answer her call.

quest:3063.text: Vengeance on the Northspring. Talo Thornhoof seeks vengeance on the Northspring harpies to the west. Once a hunter who feared no creature, Talo has hated them since they ambushed Talo in the forest. Talo Thornhoof once hunted the wild without fear. After a hard fight, Talo stayed in the forest to hone a weapon. Then harpies closed in, and Talo barely escaped to safety. Their cries still echo in Talo's memory. Talo's life was never the same, and the hatred has endured. Now Talo wants revenge. The Northspring harpies live to the west. Talo asks you to kill four Northspring Harpies, four Northspring Roguefeathers, four Northspring Windcallers and four Northspring Slayers. Their wings are black as night, Talo warns. They can vanish into the darkness.

quest:3121.text: A Strange Request. In Feralas, Witch Doctor Uzer'i sends you to Orgrimmar for a concoction. Witch Doctor Uzer'i says Neeru Fireblade in Orgrimmar has a concoction needed to begin work in Feralas. Uzer'i will not yet explain what it is for. You carry a shrunken head, promised to Neeru in exchange for the herbs. It belonged to some poor dwarf Uzer'i came across in the forest. Neeru waits in the Cleft of Shadow.

quest:3122.text: Return to Witch Doctor Uzer'i. Neeru Fireblade sends you to Witch Doctor Uzer'i in Feralas with herbs and word that he is satisfied with the shrunken head. After A Strange Request, Neeru Fireblade gives you herbs for Witch Doctor Uzer'i in Feralas. Take them to Uzer'i and tell him Neeru is satisfied with the shrunken head.

quest:3123.text: Testing the Vessel. You return to Witch Doctor Uzer'i, who tests the ritual and your skill. Now you must capture ten wildkin in the Hinterlands and bring them with the vessel back to Feralas. Witch Doctor Uzer'i tests the ritual you just performed and your own skill. The vessel Uzer'i gives you can shrink a creature and trap it inside. You travel to the Hinterlands to find wildkin. Their kind once belonged to Elune, the night elf goddess, as pets. Uzer'i names the vicious, primitive, savage owlbeasts as your quarry. Capture ten before their spirits slip away, then return with them and the vessel to Uzer'i in Feralas.

quest:3124.text: Hippogryph Muisek. In the High Wilderness, Frayfeather hippogryphs carry spirits Uzer'i wants you to capture. Their muisek can escape unless you act quickly. Witch Doctor Uzer'i trusts you with the vessel and asks you to capture another creature's spirit. Hippogryphs have long been companions to the night elves, and their spirits are loyal and steadfast. You need ten Frayfeather hippogryphs of any kind. Kill each one, then quickly shrink and capture it with the vessel to preserve its muisek. Uzer'i places them in the High Wilderness, south of the camp.

quest:3125.text: Faerie Dragon Muisek. West of Witch Doctor Uzer'i, the Horde seeks the spirits of faerie dragons. Sprite darters and sprite dragons bear the strength Uzer'i hopes to capture. Witch Doctor Uzer'i sees strength in faerie dragons, though they look delicate. They have long been allies to the night elves, and Uzer'i wants the Horde to share their power. Uzer'i gives you a Muisek Vessel and sends you west. Slay eight sprite darters or sprite dragons, then use the vessel on each fallen faerie dragon to shrink and capture its spirit.

quest:3126.text: Treant Muisek. In Feralas, Witch Doctor Uzer'i turns your search to the wandering treants. After the faerie dragons, he sends you to find three forest walkers. The night elves have made treants their allies against the Horde. Uzer'i says they move slowly, yet none can deny their strength as protectors. He means to put that strength to work for the Horde. Uzer'i asks you to find and kill three wandering forest walkers. When each treant falls, use the Muisek Vessel to shrink and capture it.

quest:3127.text:
Mountain Giant Muisek. Northwest across Feralas, you face the last creatures Witch Doctor Uzer'i hopes to harness: mountain giants. Witch Doctor Uzer'i says mountain giants came down from the mountains to aid the night elves when the Burning Legion first arrived in the world. Their immense size marks them, and rocky ground trembles beneath their steps. Uzer'i hopes to harness power on that scale.

Seven Land Walkers or Cliff Giants must fall. Then the Muisek Vessel can shrink and capture them.

quest:3128.text: Natural Materials. In Camp Mojache, Natural Materials are needed by Witch Doctor Uzer'i for an endeavor. The materials come from treants, mountain giants, faerie dragons, owlbeasts and hippogryphs, alongside the other trials. After you return to Witch Doctor Uzer'i, another list of materials awaits alongside the other trials. Bring two splintered logs from a Feralas treant. Mountain giants and faerie dragons westward carry six pieces of encrusted minerals. Owlbeasts in the Hinterlands or hippogryphs in Feralas provide twenty pieces of resilient sinew. Any of these creatures can yield the forty metallic fragments needed.

quest:3129.text: Weapons of Spirit. Witch Doctor Uzer'i is preparing weapons for you in Feralas. The work takes time, so you wait while the spirits are bound. Witch Doctor Uzer'i has the materials and the spirits you captured. Imbuing weapons with muisek takes hard work, so Uzer'i asks you to wait while the weapons are prepared.

quest:3130.text:
Against the Hatecrest. In Feathermoon Stronghold, Shandris sends you to Latronicus as she weighs the naga threat. General Shandris Feathermoon sends you to Latronicus Moonspear, her second. He has watched the naga forces closely, and Shandris must judge the wider danger they pose.

She would like to commit a full force against them. But then Feathermoon Stronghold would be open to a direct attack from the Horde, or something worse. Latronicus awaits you in the stronghold.
