quest:3161.text: Gahz'ridian. In Tanaris, Marvon Rivetseeker searches for thirty ornaments left by its old trolls. He gives you a detector of his own making to help find them. Long ago, trolls lived in Tanaris and carved ornaments in the likeness of Gahz'rilla, the hydra they revered as a god. Marvon Rivetseeker named the element in the carvings Gahz'ridian, after the hydra. He has found a few ornaments and wants more to study. Marvon Rivetseeker gives you a detector he invented to make finding Gahz'ridian easier. Wear it, and the search begins. The ornaments may lie almost anywhere in Tanaris. They are thickest near Broken Pillar, the Eastmoon Ruins and the Southmoon Ruins.

quest:3181.text: The Horn of the Beast. In Searing Gorge, Margol the Rager's horn bears a broken axe head. Margol the Rager's horn is scratched and cracked. A broken axe head is lodged in its rough surface, and Mountaineer Pebblebitty's name marks the metal. When you try to free it, the axe head shatters into a million pieces. Stonewrought Pass runs between Loch Modan and Searing Gorge. The horn begins the chain that opens the gate, and you are to take it to Mountaineer Pebblebitty. Pebblebitty is not willing to open the gate.

quest:32.text: Rise of the Silithid. In Orgrimmar, you carry Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser's report on the insect threat to Zilzibin Drumlore. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser wants the report in the hands of someone who understands such matters. Zilzibin Drumlore is a troll scholar and historian who has spent much time studying Azeroth's unique life forms. Fizzledowser hopes Zilzibin can learn what the danger is and how it might be stopped. All the help they can get will be needed. Zilzibin lives in a house on the Drag's second tier, in Orgrimmar.

quest:3362.text: Thistleshrub Valley. In Tanaris, strange beasts keep Tran'rek from entering Thistleshrub Valley. They hope to return once the creatures are cleared away. South-west of Gadgetzan, Tran'rek warns that Thistleshrub Valley is a dangerous place. Strange beasts roam there, including gnarled thistleshrubs and thistleshrub rootshapers. With so many about, Tran'rek will not return. Tran'rek asks you to clear out eight gnarled thistleshrubs and eight thistleshrub rootshapers. They also want a closer look at the cactus in the valley, so leave some of it in one piece.

quest:3367.text: Suntara Stones. In Searing Gorge, Dorius Stonetender lies badly hurt and asks you to help him reach Ironforge. Dorius Stonetender groans with pain. He feels light-headed as the world spins around him, and he is bleeding inside. He longs to return to Ironforge. So he asks you to help him make the journey.

quest:3368.text: Suntara Stones. At the Suntara Stones, Dorius's letter tells of a team enslaved by the Dark Irons. The stones are real and held by the Dark Irons. Their leader, Lathoric the Black, uses the stones' power to enslave Dorius's excavation team. You carry the letter to his brother Thorius at Ironforge's Hall of Explorers. Dorius's letter tells his brother he is gone if the message is being read. The Suntara Stones are real, and the Dark Irons hold them. Their leader, Lathoric the Black, uses their power to enslave Dorius's excavation team. The team was taken to the cauldron, where their minds are twisted as they toil day and night to finish something called Obsidion. Dorius begs his brother to help them. He calls it his final wish and asks that those who bring the letter be thanked.

quest:3372.text: Release Them. In Searing Gorge, a dying archaeologist begs you to free those still laboring under Suntara's power. Their bodies have failed, and the relic guarded by Twilight's Hammer must be placed on Suntara's altar. A dying archaeologist asks you to release those still at their labor, then collapses. Their bodies have given out, yet Suntara's power drives them on. The archaeologist says Suntara's altar is the key. Northwest of the cave, in the hills above it, Twilight's Hammer Idolaters guard the Mysterious Artifact. Take the relic from them and carry it to the Slag Pit. There, set it upon Suntara's altar.

quest:3374.text: The Essence of Eranikus. At the Oathstone, Itharius reaches you through the stone and asks you to help redeem Eranikus's corrupted soul. The first sacrifice is the gem that chains the free part of Eranikus's mind. Itharius waits in the Swamp of Sorrows. Through the Oathstone, Itharius asks you to aid Ysera's Dragonflight in redeeming Eranikus's corrupted soul. He warns that many sacrifices will be asked of you both. First, give him the gem that chains the part of Eranikus's mind still free. Take the Oathstone and the Chained Essence of Eranikus to Itharius in the Swamp of Sorrows. There, you choose whether to aid the dragonflight.

quest:3377.text: Prayer to Elune. In Searing Gorge, Zamael Lunthistle waits in a cage and asks for your help. Many years have passed since anyone visited him, and first he asks you to hear his tale. Zamael Lunthistle greets you with praise to Elune. Many years have passed since anyone came to visit him. Now he asks for your help. First, hear his tale.

quest:3378.text: Prayer to Elune. At Zamael Lunthistle's request, you seek a prayer to Elune lost among the idol worshippers. Engraved on a golden tablet, it is meant for Astarii Starseeker in Darnassus. Zamael Lunthistle's faith has awakened again. Yet he says that means little after the harm he has done to the world and its people. He expects no absolution. He asks only for his prayer to be heard, so you seek the golden tablet from the idol worshippers and carry it to Astarii Starseeker in Darnassus.

quest:338.text: The Green Hills of Stranglethorn. Across Stranglethorn Vale, loose pages from Hemet Nesingwary's novel lie scattered through the jungle. Barnil Stonepot asks you to gather them into four chapters and return them. At the expedition camp, Barnil Stonepot is troubled after Welcome to the Jungle. While he proofread Hemet Nesingwary's draft, a gale snatched its loose pages and flung them into the wild. Barnil recovered many, but others remain lost in the brush. He needs you to find them and assemble Chapter I, Chapter II, Chapter III, and Chapter IV before Nesingwary learns what happened. Once you return all four chapters, Barnil can avoid an unpleasant confrontation with Nesingwary. He hopes the restored manuscript will soon reach libraries across the world.

quest:339.text: Chapter I. In Stranglethorn, Barnil Stonepot searches the jungle for four lost pages of Hemet Nesingwary's hunting manuscript. Barnil Stonepot wants the opening passage of The Green Hills of Stranglethorn restored. He says it sets the stage for the wider story and describes Hemet Nesingwary's hunting party, including Barnil himself. Pages one, four, six, and eight are missing in the jungle. When you return the four missing leaves, Barnil pieces the first section of Hemet Nesingwary's text back together.

quest:340.text: Chapter II. In Stranglethorn Vale, Barnil Stonepot searches for leaves missing from Hemet Nesingwary's manuscript. He gathered most of them himself, but travelers must help find the rest. Barnil Stonepot has recovered many leaves from Hemet Nesingwary's scattered manuscript across Stranglethorn Vale. The second chapter follows panthers and tigers through the wilderness. Pages ten, eleven, fourteen, and sixteen remain missing, so those hunting accounts are incomplete.

quest:341.text: Chapter III. Barnil Stonepot searches Stranglethorn Vale for the missing leaves of Hemet Nesingwary's hunting manuscript. Its third chapter tells of Sir Erlgadin and Lady Rouack's first kill with a dwarven rifle. Barnil Stonepot favors this part of The Green Hills of Stranglethorn. It follows Sir Erlgadin and Lady Rouack in their early exploits, including their first kill with a dwarven rifle. Then the tale breaks off at a sharp cliffhanger. Barnil needs four leaves to restore the story: pages eighteen, twenty, twenty-one, and twenty-four. They were carried off with the rest of the manuscript and scattered across Stranglethorn Vale.

quest:342.text: Chapter IV. Barnil Stonepot is searching for the ending of Hemet Nesingwary's hunting tale in Chapter IV. Three pages are missing from the jungle. Barnil Stonepot calls the fourth chapter Hemet Nesingwary's grand finale. He needs you to find pages twenty-five, twenty-six, and twenty-seven. The three sheets lie scattered across the jungle. Without them, he cannot restore the tale's conclusion.

quest:3441.text: Divine Retribution. In Searing Gorge, Kalaran Windblade tells you how his father died and why he seeks vengeance. Stormwind would not hear his plea, so he turns to a brave adventurer. Kalaran says the filth in the cauldron killed his father. He pleaded with the Stormwind magistrate, but no one answered. He says Stormwind would rather deny this part of the world exists than send soldiers to see justice done. Kalaran wants vengeance. Only a lumbering oaf of a squire stands with him, while the Dark Iron dwarves and Ragnaros's beasts could crush him alone. So he trusts a brave adventurer to face the cauldron's denizens. For anyone who helps, he promises riches beyond all dreams.

quest:3442.text:
The Flawless Flame. In Searing Gorge, Kalaran Windblade prepares to strike where it will hurt most. He means to burn the four sentry towers, opening the way for an offensive before anyone can react. First, he needs a torch of flawless flame. After Divine Retribution, Kalaran Windblade lays out his plan. He means to burn the four sentry towers so an offensive can begin before anyone has time to react.

For that, he needs the right tool and the materials to make it. Bring Kalaran four hearts of flame and four globes of golem oil, and he will craft the torch of flawless flame. He points you toward the golems and elementals of these lands.

quest:3443.text: Forging the Shaft. After The Flawless Flame, Kalaran Windblade needs a shaft to hold its fire. Eight thorium plated daggers from the cauldron can be reforged into one. Kalaran Windblade needs a shaft and a casing to hold the flawless flame. In the cauldron, Dark Iron slavers and taskmasters wield enchanted thorium, a sturdy metal. Kalaran can break down eight of their daggers and reforge the alloy into a shaft.

quest:3444.text: The Stone Circle. Marvon Rivetseeker waits in Ratchet for a serpent-marked stone. He barely escaped the Sunken Temple, and hopes it will bring back his memories. Marvon Rivetseeker remembers the evil that touched everyone who entered the Sunken Temple. Escaping meant struggling through ooze spread across the floors. One place stayed with him: a large round room crowded with serpent statues. Marvon Rivetseeker found a round stone marked with what seems to be the same serpent symbol. He had it crated and sent to his workshop in Ratchet. Bring it to him, and he may remember more.

quest:3445.text:
The Sunken Temple. Angelas Moonbreeze points you toward a buried place and a missing scholar. Far below the earth, the Sunken Temple lies beyond any power Angelas has seen. To learn more, seek Marvon Rivetseeker, last known to be in Tanaris. Angelas Moonbreeze tells you that the Sunken Temple was driven deep beneath the earth by forces beyond anything she has seen. She sends you to Marvon Rivetseeker, a goblin who studies ancient sites with her and Troyas.

Marvon left his home in Ratchet to investigate the troll ruins of Tanaris. No word of him has come for some time.

quest:3452.text: The Flame's Casing. Kalaran Windblade seeks the last piece for the torch. A large Twilight's Hammer encampment is rumored to lie in the mountains to the northwest, where its people honor their god with symbols and idols. He wants one Symbol of Ragnaros. Kalaran Windblade says the torch needs one last piece. A large Twilight's Hammer encampment is rumored to lie in the mountains to the northwest, with symbols and idols honoring its god. Their enchantment may give the torch a magical casing. Kalaran asks you for one Symbol of Ragnaros, hoping to draw out its magic. Without a suitable source of arcane energy, the torch of retribution cannot be finished.

quest:3453.text: The Torch of Retribution. At Kalaran Windblade's side, you wait while he joins the pieces and enchants The Torch of Retribution. Kalaran Windblade needs time to join the pieces and enchant the torch. He channels magic as he works, so you wait and leave him undisturbed.

quest:3454.text: The Torch of Retribution. Kalaran Windblade has finished the torch and asks you to claim it. Kalaran Windblade says the torch must be bound to its owner. He asks you to take it up yourself.

quest:3462.text: Squire Maltrake. With the Torch of Retribution in hand, Kalaran Windblade sends you to Squire Maltrake for instructions. Kalaran Windblade sends you to Squire Maltrake. The squire will explain how to use the Torch of Retribution.

quest:3463.text: Set Them Ablaze!. In Searing Gorge, you carry Maltrake’s torch to the four sentry towers. Its flames cannot be subdued, and the towers cannot be destroyed. While they burn, guards and sentries abandon their posts, leaving the Dark Irons without their first line of defense. The Torch of Retribution burns beyond the power of any element or force to subdue. Maltrake sends you into each of the four sentry towers, North, South, East and West, to use it within the walls. Dark Iron lookouts keep watch there, so Maltrake warns you to beware.

quest:348.text: Stranglethorn Fever. In Booty Bay, Fin Fizracket grows weaker with Stranglethorn Fever. He believes he is dying and says only Mokk the Savage's heart can cure him. Fin Fizracket stammers as his strength fails. Certain he has caught Stranglethorn Fever, he says he must eat the heart of Mokk the Savage to be cured. Mokk is an elusive white beast, and only Witch Doctor Unbagwa can summon him. Fin sends you to find Unbagwa in the Spirit Den, a hidden cave on the southern cape.

quest:3481.text: Trinkets.... After Set Them Ablaze!, you find the Hoard of the Black Dragonflight in Searing Gorge. The Hoard of the Black Dragonflight waits in Searing Gorge after the towers burn. The chest looks locked, and it is yours to open.

quest:351.text: Find OOX-17/TN!. In Tanaris, you turn the knob and Find OOX-17/TN! springs to life. Oglethorpe's voice says his homing robot is missing and asks you to carry the beacon to it. A knob opens the strange egg, revealing a gnomish contraption. A voice crackles from within and names its speaker as Oglethorpe. His homing robot has gone missing. Oglethorpe has computed where it went down, near the Gaping Chasm in Tanaris, and asks you to take the beacon there.

quest:3512.text: In Eranikus' Own Words. Itharius seeks Eranikus' voice through the gem. Eranikus lies between sleep and death, caught in nightmares. The essence you gave is badly tainted, yet hope remains. Itharius sends you to eastern Winterspring. Itharius says Eranikus lies between sleep and death, caught in a weave of nightmares. The essence you gave is badly tainted, yet there may be a way to reach him. To speak through the gem, Itharius sends you to eastern Winterspring to seek one of his mortal allies. Umbranse the Spiritspeaker is the ally Itharius has in mind. Umbranse is a human who acts as a medium for the dead. Eranikus is not truly dead, but Itharius believes Umbranse may still help.

quest:3520.text: Screecher Spirits. In Steamwheedle Port, Yeh'kinya asks you to gather the spirits of Feralas vale screechers. They are kin to an ancient god, and he promises to tell you more when you bring back three essences. Yeh'kinya says the vale screechers of Feralas are kin to an ancient god. Their spirits are linked to him. He gives you a bramble wand and sends you to southern and central Feralas. Wave it over a fallen vale screecher to draw out its spirit, then touch the spirit to gather its essence. He wants three essences returned with the bramble.

quest:3566.text: Rise, Obsidion!. At the archaeologist’s gasp, you learn the truth: the rescue was a trap. They beg you to avenge them and Thorius by killing Lathoric the Black and Obsidion. Curator Thorius in Ironforge needs proof. The archaeologist can barely speak. They gasp that it was all a trap, ask forgiveness, then plead for you to kill the traitor for them and for Thorius. Lathoric the Black and Obsidion must both fall. Curator Thorius in Ironforge needs proof: one head and one heart.

quest:3625.text: Enchanted Azsharite Fel Weaponry. In Stranglethorn Vale, Galvan the Ancient prepares enchanted arms against a powerful demon. Their Felcurse is meant to weaken Razelikh the Defiler and his servitors. Just south of the path into Zul'Gurub, Galvan the Ancient works with care. Forging a blade, staff, or dagger takes patience, and haste risks a flaw. Each weapon bears the Felcurse, which can be unleashed from time to time against Razelikh the Defiler and his demonic underlings. Its weakening effect lasts for different lengths of time.

quest:3626.text: Return to the Blasted Lands. Galvan the Ancient sends you back to the Blasted Lands with your newly forged weapons. The Fallen Hero of the Horde waits there, ready to ask if you will face Razelikh. Galvan the Ancient says your hour of redemption has come. Your enchanted weapons are complete, so you carry them back to the Blasted Lands to find the Fallen Hero of the Horde. The ghostly warrior asks if you are ready to face Razelikh and his minions.

quest:379.text: Slake That Thirst. In Gadgetzan, Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle needs five Wastewander Water Pouches before he can supply the 4711-FTZ power source for your kit. The Wastewander nomads east of town carry them. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan can help with the power source your kit needs after Into the Field. First, he asks you for five Wastewander Water Pouches. The Wastewander nomads live east of Gadgetzan, and Bilgewhizzle suggests you walk up and ask one for water. He wants to hear how it goes.

quest:3821.text: Dreadmaul Rock. In the Burning Steppes, Sha'ni's platoon has been gone for more than three weeks. Thal'trak Proudtusk cannot leave his post, and asks you to learn what became of his wife. Sha'ni went to the Burning Steppes to investigate strange rituals among the Firegut ogres. More than three weeks have passed, and Goretooth has heard nothing from her platoon. He tells Thal'trak to put the matter behind him and keep to his duty. But Sha'ni is his wife, and Thal'trak will not accept that. Bound to his post, he asks you to search for her.

quest:3841.text: An Orphan Looking For a Home. Kindal Moonweaver has news for you after Darnassus: the nest was saved, but its mother died. The eggs will soon hatch, and Kindal offers you one to care for. Quentin waits by the race tracks in the Shimmering Flats of Thousand Needles. Kindal Moonweaver greets you after your return from Darnassus. The nest was saved, but its mother died before help could reach her. The eggs are close to hatching, and they need a good keeper. Kindal offers you one as a pet. Carry the egg to Quentin at the race tracks in the Shimmering Flats if you want to care for it. Quentin can tell you more. Quentin waits in Thousand Needles, though the races are not why he is there. He studies whether new, fertile soil can restore the land. He hopes to find a water source nearby. The change from Feralas to Thousand Needles seems strange to him. Quentin says strange magic was at work when it happened.

quest:3842.text:
A Short Incubation. In Thousand Needles, Quentin waits as the sprite darter egg nears hatching. The Moonweavers gave you the egg, and Quentin asks for two elixirs of fortitude so he can check its health and protect it. Quentin finds it intriguing that the Moonweavers cared for the egg, and he considers them both capable. Since they gave the egg to you, you may take responsibility for it as long as you wish. It looks almost ready to hatch, but Quentin wants to check its health and make sure it is undamaged first.

A small spell will protect the egg. Quentin has every component except two elixirs of fortitude. While he waits, he admits he is growing tempted by the races. Once he knows the egg is healthy, he will return it for you to keep.

quest:3843.text: The Newest Member of the Family. Only an hour remains to bring the fragile egg to Agnar Beastamer at Aerie Peak, before the hatchling inside dies. Quentin calls the sprite darter egg a magnificent specimen. If it survives, it will make a healthy pet. He sends you to Aerie Peak in the Hinterlands, where Agnar Beastamer can guide the final steps of incubation. The dwarf is a master animal handler, and the egg cannot go long without care. Find Agnar within an hour, or the hatchling inside will die. He lives in Wildhammer Keep.

quest:4041.text: The Videre Elixir. Bring Gregan Brewspewer an Evoroot, and he can brew the Videre Elixir. He boasts of his knowledge of herbs and alchemy. Gregan Brewspewer needs an Evoroot before he can brew your Videre Elixir. He boasts that he knows a great many things about herbs and alchemy, then begins a tale about turning the cheese meant for lunch into gold. When you walk away, he asks where you are going. Ask Gregan where to find an Evoroot.

quest:4062.text: The Rise of the Machines. In the Burning Steppes, the machines bore marks that now send you to Lotwil Veriatus. The shards bear G.L.A., with a rank marking beneath. The machines you brought down in the Burning Steppes bore Rank IV, which Theodora takes to be a low rank. So Hierophant Theodora Mulvadania sends you with a sample shard to Lotwil Veriatus, renowned among scholars of elemental sciences. Lotwil is stationed at a camp to the east, where Theodora hopes he can help with the search.

quest:4120.text: The Strength of Corruption. At Camp Mojache, Talo Thornhoof sends you north to Felwood to judge the strength of its tainted beasts. Talo Thornhoof hunts by studying the strengths of his foes. He believes knowing an enemy can turn a battle in your favor. Felwood lies north of Ashenvale, where fel has tainted the creatures. Talo fears its maddened bears and wolves have grown stronger. Face twelve Angerclaw grizzlies and twelve Felpaw ravagers there. Fel-touched creatures glow a strange green. Talo senses that fel is evil, yet very powerful.

quest:4124.text:
The Missing Courier. In Feathermoon Stronghold, Latronicus Moonspear seeks help after a courier vanishes. The courier and his parcels have been gone about a week, and the stronghold's searches found nothing. Latronicus has declared him missing in action and sends you to Ginro Hearthkindle. Latronicus Moonspear has exhausted the stronghold's search for a courier and his parcels. Both have been missing for about a week, and Latronicus has declared the courier missing in action.

Ginro Hearthkindle, Latronicus's associate, is looking for help in Feathermoon Stronghold, perhaps in his quarters. Latronicus asks you to speak with Ginro if you have time and means to spare.

quest:4125.text:
The Missing Courier. Ginro Hearthkindle searches Feralas's coast for Raschal, missing for about a week. Raschal set out for Thalanaar, planning to row down the coast. Ginro could not find the boat and asks you to search the shore for a clue. Ginro Hearthkindle believes Raschal planned to row down the coast toward Thalanaar. Raschal set out about a week ago and knows Feralas well. Raschal has served with the expeditionary forces since General Feathermoon led them here.

The route crosses southern Feralas, away from the Horde camp. Ginro could not find the boat, so it may be hidden or sunk. It could hold a clue to Raschal's whereabouts. On the mainland, the Forgotten Coast runs south from the jetty.

quest:4127.text: Boat Wreckage. Off the coast, Boat Wreckage holds a clue for Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold. A well-cared-for knife lies in the mud, and you sense something else in the water. Near the wrecked boat, you feel through the mud and find a well-cared-for knife. Whoever was aboard may have lost it when the large chunk went missing from the boat. You take the knife to Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold. Ginro asked you to bring back any clue you found, yet something else still shares the water.

quest:4129.text:
The Knife Revealed. Ginro Hearthkindle sends you to Quintis Jonespyre with the knife, seeking a reading of its past. Ginro says the reading will settle Quintis's Kalimdor Hold 'Em debt. After Boat Wreckage, Ginro Hearthkindle sends you to Quintis Jonespyre with the knife. Quintis is Feathermoon Stronghold's resident druid, and he lives in a little tree-house there.

By touching an object, Quintis can learn its past. Ginro calls this psychometry magic he does not understand and chooses not to understand, though he has seen it work. Quintis owes Ginro a Kalimdor Hold 'Em debt, and Ginro says the knife's reading will clear it. Quintis says psychometric readings drain the psyche, much like losses at Kalimdor Hold 'Em. The Stronghold calls him the King of the Bad Beats. He is unlucky at cards, yet lucky with nature's secrets.

Quintis agrees to read the knife. He hopes it will bring the breakthrough needed to uncover Raschal's fate.

quest:4130.text: Psychometric Reading. After Psychometric Reading, Quintis Jonespyre is still unsteady. His vision shows Raschal and the Woodpaw gnolls, and Quintis asks you to carry word to Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold. Quintis Jonespyre is unsteady, but his vision may help. Raschal pulls two large leather backpacks from the boat, heads inland, then returns to the boat. Gnoll scalps appear, and Quintis believes Raschal met Woodpaw gnolls. Raschal is very worried, almost terrified, and does not notice water elementals forming behind him. Then the images end. Quintis needs rest, so he asks you to tell Ginro, who needs to know.

quest:4131.text:
The Woodpaw Gnolls. In southern Feralas, you search Woodpaw camps for Raschal, the courier. After Quintis's vision, Ginro Hearthkindle sends you to find him or his belongings, though Ginro doubts the gnolls were his undoing. Ginro Hearthkindle admits the Woodpaw, whom Ginro calls “friends,” may have done for Raschal after all. Still, Ginro feels the gnolls were not responsible, and their camps are the best place to start. Ginro has no clearer plan than to search them.

Gnolls keep what they scavenge and fight over it, so they may have found the backpacks Quintis mentioned. Ginro once avoided open fighting during earlier searches. Now the vision guides you, and Ginro says to rip into them. The camps lie in southern Feralas.

quest:4135.text: The Writhing Deep. In the Writhing Deep, Raschal has gone to investigate a grave danger to Feralas. Your search for him leads there. The backpacks hold a parcel for Thalanaar and a hurried note with no recipient named. Raschal of Feathermoon wrote it after finding bug-like creatures in the Writhing Deep, south of the gnoll camps. He feared they threatened all of Feralas, so he went to investigate them himself. His note shows where he went.

quest:4265.text: Freed from the Hive. At the Writhing Deep, Raschal lives, but the Zukk'ash hive has left him deeply stunned. He needs word sent to Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold. You help a night elf down from the pod, and he begins to stir. He names himself Raschal and says the bugs overwhelmed him, leaving him paralyzed inside. Though he looks healthy, he remains deeply stunned. He asks if the Stronghold sent you. Ginro Hearthkindle waits in Feathermoon Stronghold. Tell him Raschal lives and is well.

quest:4266.text: A Hero's Welcome. General Shandris Feathermoon has asked to see you in person. Ginro Hearthkindle thinks she may thank you for aiding Feathermoon Stronghold and speak about the Zukk'ash insects you and Raschal met in southern Feralas. Ginro Hearthkindle says General Shandris Feathermoon is waiting in Feathermoon Stronghold's main compound. The reports about the Zukk'ash insects frighten him.

quest:4267.text: Rise of the Silithid. In Darnassus, a copy of Raschal's account is bound for Gracina Spiritmight. General Shandris Feathermoon gives it to you, trusting the priestess's knowledge of such creatures. General Shandris Feathermoon entrusts you with a copy of Raschal's account for Gracina Spiritmight, an associate of the Protectorate. The main report has been filed in Darnassus, where Gracina lives as a priestess in the Temple of the Moon. Shandris believes her broad knowledge of such creatures will benefit everyone who receives the account. She sends you on with good wishes and a prayer that Elune watch over all.

quest:4281.text: Thalanaar Delivery. At the Woodpaw camps, a parcel for Thalanaar still waits for its recipient. The hand-written name may guide you there. You find goods for Thalanaar in the Woodpaw gnoll camps. The small way-station lies in southeastern Feralas. A hand-written name on the parcel points you toward the person expecting the goods: Falfindel Waywarder.

quest:4297.text: Food for Baby. Agnar Beastamer will care for your egg until it hatches. Sprite darters eat meat and vegetation, and their young favor raw, juicy flanks. Agnar wants Silvermane stalker flanks for the hatchling. Agnar Beastamer says sprite darters eat meat and vegetation. Their young favor raw, juicy flanks. Agnar will care for the egg until it hatches and wants Silvermane stalker flanks for the hatchling. Without a good first meal, the newborn might not live through its first week. Agnar never learned why sprite darters eat meat. Agnar knows only that it is tied to Elune’s plan for the elves. Perhaps they were meant to be protectors, Agnar wonders, but cannot say for sure. Agnar also admits to being jealous that you got the egg.

quest:4298.text: Becoming a Parent. In the Hinterlands, Agnar Beastamer has news: the egg is further along than he expected. He wants to speak with you. The egg has advanced further than Agnar Beastamer expected. You have brought food for the hatchling. Now speak with Agnar in the Hinterlands.

quest:4449.text: Caught!. In Searing Gorge, someone is calling for help from a locked outhouse. The voice inside asks you to teach eight Dark Iron geologists a lesson and bring fifteen pieces of silk cloth, though they offer no reason. The occupant fled the Dark Iron dwarves and hid in the outhouse. They believe the geologists saw them slip inside and used their magic to lock the door before they could get away. The trapped person asks you to teach eight Dark Iron geologists a lesson and bring fifteen pieces of silk cloth. When you ask why, they stumble over their words, then say it is for nothing in particular.

quest:4450.text: Ledger from Tanaris. In Searing Gorge, a small job from Tanaris now waits for you. Krinkle Goodsteel of Gadgetzan wants several things gathered here and elsewhere, then brought to him. The person inside the wooden outhouse has been helped and remembers a small job from Tanaris. Krinkle Goodsteel of Gadgetzan wants several things gathered, some in Searing Gorge and others farther away. The ledger will be slid beneath the door. Carry it and everything listed to Goodsteel in Tanaris. Goodsteel's ledger calls for twenty solid crystal leg shafts from the glassweb spiders of Searing Gorge. It also lists an overdue package at the crashed zeppelin in Beezil's Wreck, in Dustwallow Marsh. The third item is Goodsteel's balanced flameberge. Jarquia, a murloc along the eastern shore of the Swamp of Sorrows, has it.

quest:4451.text: The Key to Freedom. In Searing Gorge, you have a small brass key with no known destination. Its head reads Dark Iron Outhouse and warns against copying it. The small brass key is marked Dark Iron Outhouse, with a warning not to duplicate it. Where it leads remains unknown. Search Searing Gorge for a place that accepts it.

quest:4496.text: Bungle in the Jungle. In Gadgetzan, Alchemist Pestlezugg studies the silithid and likens them to bees. He believes their queen is the weak point, and needs scent and soil from Un'Goro Crater to the west. Alchemist Pestlezugg likens the silithid to bees. He believes that if their queen is destroyed, the rest will fall into disarray. A lure can draw her out. You are to bring her down when she appears. To make the lure, Pestlezugg needs reagents from Un'Goro Crater. The silithid hive lies west of Gadgetzan. He asks you to bring an undamaged scent gland from one of the bugs and five samples of the native soil.

quest:4504.text: Super Sticky. In Gadgetzan, Tran'rek sees quick gold in super sticky glue. He needs tar from beasts near the pits in northern Un'Goro Crater and offers a little of the profit. Tran'rek hopes his newest idea will bring quick gold, and offers you a little of the profit. Ordinary tar is not sticky enough. He wants twelve samples from creatures near the tar pits in northern Un'Goro Crater. The plant-like creatures around the pits have chlorophyll in their skin. Mixed with tar, it makes a super sticky glue.

quest:4507.text: Pawn Captures Queen. Alchemist Pestlezugg sends you into Un'Goro Crater with a lure for the Gorishi Hive Queen. After Bungle in the Jungle, he wants her brain brought to Gadgetzan for study. Pestlezugg gives you a lure for the silithid hive. He believes a crystal in the hive network attunes the whole swarm, and the hatcheries are the best place to search. Apply the lure to the crystal, and the queen should emerge with several guards beside her. Pestlezugg wants you to carry the queen's brain to Gadgetzan. He knows it sounds icky, but says the brain is badly needed for study.

quest:4508.text: Calm Before the Storm. After the queen falls, you carry the latest findings from Un'Goro beyond Gadgetzan. Alchemist Pestlezugg sends the report to Gracina Spiritmight at the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Alchemist Pestlezugg says Gadgetzan cannot face the silithid alone. The latest findings from Un'Goro must reach someone who can act on them, so you carry the report to Gracina Spiritmight in Darnassus. Pestlezugg hopes she is at the Temple of the Moon. She has friends among the Alliance's leading figures, and drawing them in may offer a way through this alive.

quest:4509.text: Calm Before the Storm. After the queen's fall, Alchemist Pestlezugg sends his latest findings to those who may act. You carry his report on Un'Goro to Zilzibin Drumlore in Orgrimmar. Gadgetzan cannot manage alone, so Alchemist Pestlezugg sends you with his latest findings on Un'Goro. He wants them in the hands of those who can act. Pestlezugg expects Zilzibin Drumlore to be in the upper part of the Drag in Orgrimmar. Zilzibin has friends high in the Horde, and drawing them in may offer a way through this alive.

quest:4787.text: The Ancient Egg. In Tanaris, Yeh'kinya seeks the ancient egg named in the Prophecy of Mosh'aru. It comes from the age of troll empires, and he wants you to bring it from Jintha'Alor in the Hinterlands. The Prophecy of Mosh'aru tells of an ancient egg from the age when trolls ruled vast empires. Its power can contain Hakkar's essence. Yeh'kinya believes it may be the only way to guard the world from his evil. Yeh'kinya asks you to bring the egg to Tanaris. Tales place it deep inside Jintha'Alor in the Hinterlands, in a cave behind the amphitheater atop the city. Great forces stir, and Yeh'kinya fears time is running short.

quest:485.text: Find OOX-09/HL!. Near Skulk Rock, a homing robot lies crashed in the Hinterlands. Its gnomish maker, Oglethorpe Obnoticus, calls through a metal egg and asks you to carry a beacon to the wreck. Turn the knob on the strange metal egg, and a gnomish device opens. A crackling voice gives the name Oglethorpe Obnoticus. His homing robot has crashed, and he has worked out where it came down: where the river begins, near Skulk Rock. Carry the beacon there. At the river's head, you find wreckage shaped like a robotic chicken. Oglethorpe Obnoticus confirms that it is his homing robot. It needs a jump start before it can return to Booty Bay for repairs. Place the beacon inside.

quest:504.text: Crushridge Warmongers. In the Ruins of Alterac, Crushridge Warmongers face a fiercer hunt. Marshal Redpath of Southshore sends you after them to keep the ogres from Alliance lands. Marshal Redpath sends you into the Ruins of Alterac after Crushridge Bounty. He wants you to hunt down many Crushridge Warmongers and strike the Crushridge ogres hard. Redpath believes nothing else will teach the brutes to keep clear of Alliance territory.

quest:507.text: Lord Aliden Perenolde. Krusk sends you north to Lord Aliden Perenolde's manor by Lordamere Lake. Once Perenolde is dead, his mistress Elysa can tell you about the Warchief's pendant. After Blackmoore's Legacy, Krusk sends you to end Perenolde's foulness. His manor stands at Dandred's Fold, on the shores of Lordamere Lake to the north. Once Perenolde is dead, ask his mistress Elysa about Taretha's pendant. The Warchief desires it.

quest:508.text: Taretha's Gift. Elysa gives up Taretha's Gift and asks for peace. After the step with Lord Aliden Perenolde, you carry the pendant to Krusk in Tarren Mill. Elysa wants no memory of Lord Aliden Perenolde. She gives you the pendant and asks only to be left in peace. It once belonged to Taretha Foxton, Thrall's childhood friend. You carry it to Krusk in Tarren Mill, returning it to the orcs.

quest:519.text: The Crown of Will. In Tarren Mill, Melisara seeks three ogre heads before Mug'Thol's. Melisara names Targ, Muckrake and Glommus as Mug'Thol's loyal lieutenants. She wonders what could make an ogre loyal. Kill all three and bring their heads to Tarren Mill. Then Mug'Thol's head, crown and all, is the only one left to take.

quest:520.text: The Crown of Will. Melisara in Tarren Mill sends you after Mug'Thol, whose lieutenants are dead. Bring back his head and the Crown of Will, and the Crushridge resistance will be over. Only Mug'Thol remains. Melisara expects him to resist giving up the Crown of Will. With his lieutenants fallen, he likely expects you. Find him, kill him, and bring his head and the Crown back to Tarren Mill.

quest:521.text: The Crown of Will. Melisara sends the Crown of Will to the Undercity, where Sharlindra will see it reaches Lady Sylvanas. Melisara sends you with the Crown to Sharlindra in the Undercity. Sharlindra will pass it on to Lady Sylvanas. Melisara warns you not to use the Crown for your own ends. Mug'Thol's fate is warning enough.

quest:523.text:
Baron's Demise. In Southshore, Magistrate Henry Maleb seeks justice for the contract you recovered. Baron Vardus, a cold-hearted nobleman of old Alterac, signed it, and Maleb asks you to bring him his head. After Assassin's Contract, Magistrate Henry Maleb tells you Baron Vardus signed the contract. Vardus is a nobleman of old Alterac, known for his cold heart and brutal ways. Maleb is not surprised to find him behind it. Southshore will not let the baron send thugs against the town without answering for it.

Maleb thinks Vardus may be among the Syndicate's haunts, in Strahnbrad's ruins or the valley north of them. He asks you to bring him the baron's head.

quest:537.text:
Dark Council. In Southshore, Magistrate Henry Maleb weighs a letter naming Nagaz and the Argus Wake. He fears they may threaten the land if allied with the Syndicate, and sends you to hunt Nagaz and the Argus Shadow Mages in the Uplands. After Further Mysteries, Maleb tells you the letter came from Nagaz, who belongs to the Argus Wake. He does not know what the Argus Wake is, but fears an alliance with the Syndicate would make them a threat. So he wants Nagaz and the Argus Shadow Mages named in the letter found and killed. Bring him Nagaz’s head.

Search the Uplands, north of Strahnbrad, where the Syndicate is strongest. Maleb hopes the Argus Wake’s envoys are there.

quest:551.text: The Ensorcelled Parchment. At the top of The Ensorcelled Parchment, Nagaz is the only name clear. A spell hides the rest, so you take it to Loremaster Dibbs in Southshore. A spell keeps the parchment's writing from being read. Only Nagaz can be made out at the top. You take it to Loremaster Dibbs in Southshore.

quest:554.text: Stormpike's Deciphering. In Ironforge, Loremaster Dibbs sends you to Prospector Stormpike with an ensorcelled parchment. After The Ensorcelled Parchment, Dibbs sends you to Ironforge with the parchment. Prospector Stormpike is studying at the Prospector headquarters. Tell him Dibbs sent you; Dibbs has been bringing Stormpike plenty of business lately.

quest:566.text: WANTED: Baron Vardus. In Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia calls for Baron Vardus's death. He is a human and a high-ranking member of the Syndicate, accused of crimes against the Forsaken. Bring Darthalia proof of his death. High Executor Darthalia has set a price on Baron Vardus. He is a human accused of crimes against the Forsaken and one of the Syndicate's high-ranking members. Word last placed him in the Uplands of the Alterac Mountains, north of Tarren Mill. Darthalia calls for his death, and payment awaits whoever brings her proof. Baron Vardus may be at any of the Syndicate camps across the Uplands. He may also be hiding in the cellar of the inn at Strahnbrad.

quest:571.text: Mok'thardin's Enchantment. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Far Seer Mok'thardin needs a strong binding for the Stranglethorn trophies gathered so far. Aged sinew from elder primates in southern Stranglethorn Vale will hold the feathers, claws, and fang fast. The feathers, claws, and pristine fang bring Far Seer Mok'thardin to the next stage of his ritual. He needs a tough magical tether to bind them together. Only aged sinew from an Elder Mistvale Gorilla can endure the magic he plans to weave. Elder Mistvale Gorillas forage in the jungles east of Booty Bay. Mok'thardin needs flawless sinew, so you may have to hunt several before finding one fit for his enchantment.

quest:572.text: Mok'thardin's Enchantment. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Far Seer Mok'thardin gathers materials for a shamanistic ritual. With feline trophies collected, he now seeks feathers from Stranglethorn Vale's raptors. Far Seer Mok'thardin still needs more before his shamanistic ritual can begin. He is gathering materials for a tool to aid the Warchief. Now he asks you to bring feathers worn by Jungle Stalkers. The raptors live in the dense jungle south of Grom'gol Base Camp, near the great arena.

quest:573.text: Mok'thardin's Enchantment. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Far Seer Mok'thardin seeks the last sacred water for a ceremonial choker. He sends you to a Holy Spring on the southern bluffs near the western sea, where naga explorers have arrived. Far Seer Mok'thardin needs water from a Holy Spring high above Stranglethorn Vale's southern bluffs, near the western coast. You have helped with the earlier stages of the enchantment. Scholars of the mystic and divine dispute who the spring was sanctified for. Every race across Azeroth claims its holy waters were meant for its own people. Naga explorers have reached the spring, and Mok'thardin needs you to drive them away. Bring him a draught of the water and slay ten of the serpent intruders. He needs both to finish the ceremonial choker in the Warchief's name.

quest:576.text: Keep An Eye Out. In Booty Bay, Dizzy One-Eye needs the enchanted eye that gives him sight. Bloodsail Buccaneers ambushed him last night and took it. Dizzy One-Eye lost both eyes in battle. Later, his ship docked at Menethil, where a traveling wizard made him an enchanted glass eye. It restored his sight, and Dizzy once kept watch from the crow’s nest. Without it, he feels useless. Bloodsail Buccaneers ambushed Dizzy as he was leaving last night and took his eye. Their presence in Booty Bay troubles him. He fears the captain will keelhaul him when the eye’s fate comes out. A lookout who cannot see may be fit only to scrub the bilge, he reckons. So he asks you to get the eye back from the Bloodsail Buccaneers.

quest:580.text: Whiskey Slim's Lost Grog. In Booty Bay, Whiskey Slim needs twelve bottles of Pupellyverbos Port back before his ship sails. His crew seized the crate from a privateer, and he fears a flogging if his commanding officer finds it missing. Off the Overlook Cliffs, Whiskey Slim's ship was caught in severe weather with the Hinterlands shore nearby. The crew had seized a crate of Pupellyverbos Port from a privateer bound for Stormwind. As waves threatened to swallow the ship, Slim broke into the captain's crate for courage. Then a sudden surge swept the bottles overboard. Back in Booty Bay, Whiskey Slim's ship is preparing to weigh anchor. He fears the cat-o'-nine-tails when his commanding officer discovers the confiscated port is missing. Slim needs someone to bring back twelve bottles before his theft comes to light.

quest:5801.text: Fire Plume Forged. At Fire Plume Ridge, you face the heat needed to forge a skeletal key stem. The simmering volcano lies west in Un'Goro Crater, where its lava lake can fuse the stem. Then you carry it to Alchemist Arbington at Chillwind Point in the Western Plaguelands. Krinkle Goodsteel says the key stem needs two bars of thorium and fierce heat. You find the thorium, and your gold buys a mold. Dip it in the lava lake atop Fire Plume Ridge. There, the heat fuses thorium and bone together. Krinkle Goodsteel has done their part. To finish the key, you return to Alchemist Arbington at Chillwind Point in the Western Plaguelands. The lava-forged stem remains unfinished. This work prepares you for an assault.

quest:5802.text: Fire Plume Forged. At Fire Plume Ridge, fierce heat can forge the stem of a skeletal key. Krinkle Goodsteel sends you to the volcano west in Un'Goro Crater, where a lava lake crowns its summit. You then carry the stem to Apothecary Dithers at the Bulwark in the Western Plaguelands. Two bars of thorium and fierce heat are needed to forge the key stem. You find the thorium, and Krinkle Goodsteel helps provide the heat. Your gold has bought a mold, ready for the lava lake atop Fire Plume Ridge. There, lava fuses thorium and bone together. Krinkle Goodsteel has done their part. Now you return to Apothecary Dithers at the Bulwark in the Western Plaguelands to finish the key. The stem forged in lava remains unfinished, and this work prepares for an assault.

quest:584.text: Bloodscalp Clan Heads. Nimboya still seeks word of Yenniku after the trophies are sorted. The young troll is missing, so the Darkspear turn to the Bloodscalp Clan Heads for answers. Nimboya seeks answers from the Bloodscalp leaders. The earlier hunt found no sign of Yenniku among the fallen. Gan'zulah, the Bloodscalp chief, and Nezzliok the Dire, his witch doctor, are enemies of the Darkspear. Neither would speak willingly. So Nimboya plans to bring their heads to the cauldron at Grom'gol Base Camp and force the truth from their dead lips. Gan'zulah and Nezzliok dwell deep in the ruins of Zul'Kunda in northwestern Stranglethorn Vale. Nimboya means to cast their heads into the boiling brew and make them speak about Yenniku.

quest:585.text: Speaking with Nezzliok. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Nezzliok's severed head speaks from a bubbling cauldron. The Bloodscalp witch doctor knows where Yenniku was taken, but demands a grim tribute before he tells you. Nezzliok remains bound in the bubbling cauldron after the hunt for Bloodscalp Clan Heads. He knows where Yenniku was taken, but gives up nothing freely. Bring three trophy skulls from the rival Skullsplitter tribe to his resting place. Then his departed spirit can command thralls in the Nether. Nezzliok demands one skull from the Skullsplitter trophy pile at Balia'mah, one from Ziata'jai, and one from Zul'Mamwe. All three offerings must lie beside his own head before the dead witch doctor will consider his spirit satisfied.

quest:586.text: Speaking with Gan'zulah. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Gan'zulah curses those who stand over the bubbling pot. The Bloodscalp chieftain demands the deaths of his Skullsplitter rivals and the ruin of their ruler, Ana'thek the Cruel. Gan'zulah's severed head curses anyone who stands over the bubbling pot. Though dead, the Bloodscalp chieftain still hates his captors and ancestral enemies. He points you east toward the Skullsplitter stronghold and demands the deaths of its hunters, headhunters, and berserkers. Their ferocious warband may kill those who dare face it. Gan'zulah expects the assault to end in disaster. He believes Chief Ana'thek the Cruel will tear apart any intruder who challenges him. Still, he demands Ana'thek's shattered armor as proof of triumph. Bring that trophy back to the cauldron at Grom'gol Base Camp to satisfy Gan'zulah's spite.

quest:5863.text: The Dunemaul Compound. In the desert south of Gadgetzan, a growing ogre force has Andi Lynn afraid. She wants the compound destroyed before the ogres gather more strength. A large band of nomadic ogres has reached Tanaris. South of Gadgetzan, they have claimed a broad stretch of desert and made their compound. Smaller bands roam the desert, and some have entered the old troll ruins. Andi Lynn fears what may happen if the ogres grow stronger. Andi Lynn wants ten Dunemaul Brutes and ten Dunemaul Enforcers cut down. Gor'marok the Ravager leads the band. Andi Lynn believes the ogres will begin to crumble once he no longer commands them.

quest:587.text:
Up to Snuff. In Booty Bay, Deeg is waiting for the snuff he likes, but the herbalist has none to sell. Bloodsail Raiders are said to have taken the shipment, and Deeg asks you to bring him fifteen shares. Deeg knows life at sea may be poor, yet it is the only life he has. Whenever he reaches port, he looks for grog and fine snuff.

The Booty Bay herbalist has run out. The herbalist says Bloodsail Raiders hijacked the shipment, so Deeg hopes a fearless traveler can persuade them to share it. He wants fifteen shares of snuff.

quest:588.text: The Fate of Yenniku. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Nezzliok's head speaks of Yenniku from the cauldron. Kin'weelay waits beside it for the spirit's words. You've appeased the spirits of Gan'zulah and Nezzliok. Now Nezzliok's head speaks from the bubbling cauldron. Kin'weelay waits beside it to hear the secret.

quest:589.text: The Singing Crystals. Kin'weelay seeks a way to free Yenniku from the darkness holding him. He turns to the Mind's Eye and asks you to gather shards that may help him command its power. Kin'weelay searches old jungle lore for a way to free Yenniku's spirit. The tales speak of the Mind's Eye, a gem hidden deep in Stranglethorn and mighty in magic. Kin'weelay believes it may hold the answer. As he seeks the jungle spirits' guidance to find it, he needs rare catalysts to control its sorcery safely. Kin'weelay sends you southeast to Crystalvein Mine, where ironjaw basilisks dwell beneath the earth. He asks you to recover three pulsing blue shards from them. He plans to channel the magic in these singing stones during a final ritual. Once he has recovered the Mind's Eye, he means to bend its power to his will.

quest:591.text: The Mind's Eye. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Kin'weelay seeks The Mind's Eye to save Yenniku. Mai'Zoth holds the gem deep in the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound. After the singing crystals are recovered, Kin'weelay turns to The Mind's Eye. He believes only the gem can help save Yenniku, son of the Darkspear chieftain. Mai'Zoth holds it. Kin'weelay remembers the ogre mage from the Darkspear tribe's earlier days in the jungle. Mai'Zoth dwells deep in the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound, east of Grom'gol. His magic was formidable before he took The Mind's Eye, and the stone has made him stronger still. The ogre stronghold is perilous. Yet the gem is the young troll's only hope of freedom.

quest:592.text: Saving Yenniku. Kin'weelay has found a way to bring Yenniku home from Zanzil the Outcast. He reshapes the recovered Mind's Eye into a soul gem that can stun Yenniku and hold his spirit until you take it to Nimboya. Kin'weelay turns the recovered Mind's Eye into a magical soul gem. Its enchantment lets you stun Yenniku and set the stone on his head to capture his spirit. With Yenniku's spirit inside, you can carry the gem safely to his kin at Grom'gol Base Camp. Zanzil the Outcast holds Yenniku in the Ruins of Aboraz, along the Crystal Shore on the southern Cape of Stranglethorn. You enter Zanzil's territory and use the gem to break the witch doctor's hold over the young troll. Then you carry the filled gem back to Nimboya.

quest:593.text: Filling the Soul Gem. In Stranglethorn Vale, you reach Yenniku while he remains caught in a trance. A prepared soul gem may preserve him by taking his spirit. Yenniku, the young troll you have tried to save, stands motionless before you in Stranglethorn Vale. His mind is far away. The enchanted gem prepared to hold his essence is the only path forward.

quest:594.text: Message in a Bottle. Along Stranglethorn Vale's shore, Message in a Bottle bears a plea from someone held captive. The writer says a great beast keeps them on an isolated island in the South Seas. A plea for rescue rests in a glass container, half-buried in the sand. The captive is trapped beneath thick jungle canopies on a foreign island, held by a great Skymane. Wild Shore lies to the northwest through the trees. Large sailing vessels drift to the southwest.

quest:595.text: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. Along the Savage Coast, rumors of rival pirates trouble the newly arrived Blackwater Raiders. First Mate Crazz sends you to scout a cove while his crew drinks and seeks company in Booty Bay. The Blackwater Raiders have just docked in Booty Bay when word reaches them of rivals across southern Stranglethorn Vale. The crew is busy with grog and company ashore, so First Mate Crazz asks you to go in their place. Head north along the Savage Coast and scout a cove for signs of what the Bloodsail Buccaneers are doing.

quest:597.text: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. At Booty Bay, the Bloodsail Buccaneers’ plans now point to a camp and an attack signal. A map marks the Bloodsail Buccaneers’ intended camp in Booty Bay with a red X. Their orders call for silence. The crew must kill anyone who approaches and wait for a signal from the southern command post before attacking. You carry the findings back to First Mate Crazz in Booty Bay. He sent you to scout, and the pirates are still waiting for the signal before they attack.

quest:598.text: Split Bone Necklace. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp sends you southeast to hunt the Skullsplitters. The Darkspears left Stranglethorn Vale, yet their old feud with these jungle rivals continues. Bring back twenty-five split bone trophies to aid the Darkspears and earn their friendship. After the Bloodscalp hunt, Kin'weelay turns to another old enemy. Southeast of Grom'gol Base Camp, the Skullsplitter tribe has fought the Darkspears for many years. The Darkspears no longer live in Stranglethorn Vale, yet they remain bound to this war. You travel into Skullsplitter territory to claim twenty-five split bone necklaces and earn the Darkspears' friendship and respect. Kin'weelay takes pride in seeing these hostile trolls cut down like young saplings by a basilisk. Each trophy you bring back counts as a victory for his people.

quest:599.text: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. First Mate Crazz has learned that the Bloodsail Buccaneers mean to strike Booty Bay. He sends you to warn Fleet Master Seahorn, commander of the Blackwater Raiders, before they move. First Mate Crazz sends you to warn Fleet Master Seahorn of an attack on Booty Bay. Crazz has learned the Bloodsail Buccaneers mean to strike the port directly, and the threat is greater than he first thought. Seahorn is somewhere in town. He must hear the warning before the rival pirates move.

quest:600.text: Venture Company Mining. In northern Stranglethorn, the Venture Company keeps finding Singing Blue Crystals. Crank Fizzlebub in Booty Bay wants ten brought back from the hills near Crystalvein Mine. You’ve gathered Singing Blue Shards, and now Crank Fizzlebub points you toward a larger rival. The Venture Company’s work across the jungle cuts into the profits of independent goblins. Basilisks keep its miners out of Crystalvein Mine, so they dig in the hills around it for Singing Blue Crystals. Crank asks you to take ten from the miners and bring them to Booty Bay as proof of their setback.

quest:604.text: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. On the Wild Shore, the Bloodsail Buccaneers have raised a southern command post. Fleet Master Seahorn sends a trusted Blackwater Raider to seize their charts and orders, so the fleet can learn their plans. Crazz’s praise has brought you to Fleet Master Seahorn’s notice. The Bloodsail Buccaneers have raised a southern command post on the Wild Shore. Seahorn sends you to strike their camp, cut down their swashbucklers, and seize their naval charts and written orders. The fleet needs those papers to learn what its rivals intend.

quest:606.text: Scaring Shaky. At Booty Bay's docks, “Shaky” Phillipe still owes “Sea Wolf” MacKinley from last week's game. MacKinley sends you outside town for Elder Mistvale Gorilla giblets to frighten Phillipe into paying. “Sea Wolf” MacKinley wants his gambling debts paid, and many people owe him. “Shaky” Phillipe is first. He waits by the docks in Booty Bay and owes a large sum from last week's game. MacKinley sends you outside town to hunt Elder Mistvale Gorillas and bring back plenty of giblets. Keep their animal origin quiet, so Phillipe imagines the worst.

quest:607.text: Return to MacKinley. You carry Phillipe’s pouch to Sea Wolf MacKinley, who is owed payment. Phillipe says he meant to pay all along and asks that you go easy. "Shaky" Phillipe hands you a pouch of payment for Sea Wolf MacKinley. He swears he always meant to repay the debt. Phillipe says he got a little drunk and lost the way. He thinks MacKinley will understand, and insists there is no need to get rough.

quest:608.text: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. In Stranglethorn, the Bloodsail Buccaneers gather strength for an attack. Fleet Master Seahorn will not risk his whole fleet in a counterstrike, so he sends a small crew against their leaders before they can begin. Fleet Master Seahorn means to halt the Bloodsail attack before it gains strength. He mocks Fleet Master Firallon's skill at sea, then chooses to strike at the commanders. Seahorn will not risk a full naval battle. Instead, he sends a small crew to Firallon's landing camp to kill Firallon, Captain Stillwater, and Captain Keelhaul. Without their leaders, the buccaneers will be left without command.

quest:609.text: Voodoo Dues. In Booty Bay, “Sea Wolf” MacKinley is still waiting for three old debts to be paid. Maury “Club Foot” Wilkins, Jon-Jon the Crow, and Chucky “Ten Thumbs” owe him, but rumors say curses and enchantment sent them wandering ancient jungle ruins. MacKinley wants their prized possessions, whatever their fate. You have already collected debts for “Sea Wolf” MacKinley, but three accounts remain unpaid. Maury “Club Foot” Wilkins, Jon-Jon the Crow, and Chucky “Ten Thumbs” have owed him for months. MacKinley first thought they had left Booty Bay to escape their debts. Then he heard they had met a stranger, darker fate deep in the jungle. Whispers say curses and enchantment have left the three men wandering ancient stonework northeast of Booty Bay. They are said to roam the Ruins of Aboraz and the Ruins of Jubuwal. MacKinley wants you to find each man and take his notable valuables: Jon-Jon's Golden Spyglass, Chucky's Huge Ring, and Maury's Clubbed Foot.

quest:611.text: The Curse of the Tides. Off Stranglethorn's coast, Catelyn the Blade lends you her recovered knife to strike a sunken altar. Baron Revilgaz in Booty Bay seeks the Stone of the Tides for his collection of ancient troll artifacts. Catelyn the Blade lends you her recovered troll dagger to break an altar beneath the waves. She knows less of troll ruins than her father, but has heard of a sunken troll city. So she points you northwest of Grom'gol Base Camp. There, in the Vile Reef's underwater ruins, the Altar of the Tides glows blue among sea life and murlocs.

quest:613.text: Cracking Maury's Foot. At Booty Bay, MacKinley still cannot claim what Maury owed him. Maury locked the debt inside his own foot, so MacKinley sends travelers to the Mosh'Ogg ogre mound in Stranglethorn Vale to find the key. After the foot was recovered in Voodoo Dues, "Sea Wolf" MacKinley faces another obstacle in Booty Bay. His late debtor locked the foot, sealing the valuables he owes inside. Maury gambled with the ogres at the Mosh'Ogg mound northeast of Booty Bay. MacKinley recalls Maury saying they drove him away after he won too much. So MacKinley suspects they have the key and sends you to search for it.

quest:617.text: Akiris by the Bundle. In Booty Bay, Privateer Bloads seeks akiris reeds for an associate who pays well. The naga were last seen on the northern beach, where you must take the reeds from them. Privateer Bloads offers seaside work in Booty Bay. His associate Groy pays well for bundles of akiris reed, a plant that grows by the sea and bears the name the naga give it. Bloads does not know why Groy wants the reeds. He needs ten stalks, and the naga were last seen on the northern beach.

quest:618.text: Facing Negolash. Along Stranglethorn Vale's coast, a stolen cutlass sets events in motion. Sprogger knows how to draw Negolash out with the giant's favorite food and drink. When giants wrecked Captain Smotts' vessel, Negolash headed for the galley. He left the crew alone and went after wine and Barbecued Buzzard Wings, Sprogger's specialty. Sprogger had traveled to the Badlands to learn the recipe. Sprogger plans to lure Negolash with a feast. You carry ten servings of wings and five bottles of wine to Captain Smotts' ruined lifeboat on the southeastern shore. The banquet draws the giant near. Then you can confront him and reclaim the captain's cutlass.

quest:619.text: Enticing Negolash. Along Stranglethorn Vale's shore, a marked lifeboat offers a way to lure Negolash. Ten barbecued buzzard wings and five bottles of junglevine wine lie on the wreck. The abandoned lifeboat bears the faded words Smotts' Revenge. While hunting Negolash, arrange ten barbecued buzzard wings and five bottles of junglevine wine on the wreck to draw him out.

quest:621.text: Zanzil's Secret. Crank Fizzlebub seeks Zanzil's Secret in the ruins northeast of Booty Bay. The exiled troll's brew bends minds and strengthens bodies, and Crank wants samples for himself. Northeast of Booty Bay, Zanzil has made his home in the ruins of Jubuwal and Aboraz. His former tribal leaders cast him out, fearing his mastery over other minds. Now he rules followers with concoctions made from jungle plants. The mixtures dull their will and heighten their strength, leaving them docile but sturdy. Crank Fizzlebub sees profit in Zanzil's craft. Those who want power over others might pay handsomely for such a brew, so the goblin wants a supply from the ruins. Deliver enough samples and Crank offers the usual coin, with a quiet bonus if you keep the bargain private.

quest:623.text: Akiris by the Bundle. In Stranglethorn Vale, Bloads has a fresh bundle of akiris reeds bound for Theramore Isle. His contact, Privateer Groy, has a client eager for more, but Bloads cannot sail to Dustwallow Marsh for another week. While you are away, word reaches you from across the sea. Privateer Groy in Theramore Isle is pleased with the last shipment of akiris reeds, and a client wants another bundle at once. Privateer Bloads cannot sail to Dustwallow Marsh for another week. So he gives you the parcel to carry across the sea by hand.

quest:624.text: Cortello's Riddle. A parchment bearing Cortello's Riddle turns up aboard Bloodsail Buccaneer vessels along the Wild Shore. Its verse sends you toward a clue beneath an ornate bridge. Bloodsail Buccaneers anchored off Stranglethorn Vale's southern coast carry scattered notes with a rhyme. Cortello's verse describes a finely worked bridge, worn by many travelers. It lies east of Deadwind and south of Redridge. Follow the directions out of the jungle and into the marshes, where something waits below.

quest:625.text: Cortello's Riddle. Travelers follow Cortello's second verse across the sea to Kalimdor. Its lines point treasure hunters toward a cave in southwestern Dustwallow Marsh. Cortello's second verse sends searchers toward Kalimdor. It describes Dustwallow Marsh, a gloomy wetland east of the Barrens. The riddle points to a clue in a cave in the southwest of the marsh.

quest:626.text: Cortello's Riddle. In the Hinterlands, the final verses of Cortello's Riddle draw treasure hunters to the coast. A musty scroll points north from the southern tropics, and the trail ends beneath the waterfalls. The weathered verse turns the search north, away from the southern tropics and toward Lordaeron. There, amid the great turmoil of the embattled lands, the long chase reaches its end along the coast. The final hoard lies along the Hinterlands shore. Search underwater at the foot of the great falls.

quest:630.text: Message in a Bottle. The message in a bottle brings you to an island off the Stranglethorn coast, where Princess Poobah waits in chains. King Mukla commands the island’s beasts and keeps her captive. To free her, you need the key to her shackle. On an island off the Stranglethorn coast, Princess Poobah waits in chains. The message in the bottle has brought you to her. King Mukla is a great Skymane gorilla who commands the creatures roaming the island. He keeps Poobah imprisoned, and she trusts you to face the ape and bring back her shackle key. Princess Poobah says her captor often prowls the island’s southeastern side. King Mukla is a formidable foe. Defeating him is the only way to claim the shackle key and free Poobah.

quest:640.text: The Broken Sigil. Zengu sends you to recover sigils from the Stromgarde militia. Galen, son of Thoras Trollbane, broke the Sigil of Thoradin into eleven pieces, and you carry them to Tor'gan in Hammerfall. Three sigils guard Thoras Trollbane's tomb. You have taken the first from the Syndicate. The firmly entrenched Stromgarde militia holds the other two. Galen, Thoras' son, broke the Sigil of Thoradin into eleven pieces and scattered them among the defenders. Zengu asks you to gather the pieces from Stromgarde's defenders. Then carry them to Tor'gan, the troll shaman at Hammerfall. He can bind them into a whole sigil.

quest:641.text: Sigil of Thoradin. Tor'gan has restored the Sigil of Thoradin, and Zengu waits in Hammerfall for its return. The sigil can open the seal on Trollbane's tomb. Tor'gan's reconstruction has worked. The Sigil of Thoradin can open the seal on Trollbane's tomb, so he sends you back to Zengu in Hammerfall. Zengu has more for you to do.

quest:643.text: Sigil of Arathor. Zengu sends you from Hammerfall to seek a sigil carried by human cavalry in the Arathi Highlands. Find their leader, Lieutenant Valorcall, and bring the sigil back. Zengu doubts the humans can claim Stromgarde, much less the whole Arathi Highlands. Yet their prince still sends the last of his horsemen through the countryside. Zengu cannot see why. He knows Lieutenant Valorcall leads those riders and carries one of the sigils. Find Valorcall and bring it back to Hammerfall.

quest:644.text: Sigil of Trollbane. In Hammerfall, Zengu sends you deep into Stromgarde for the Sigil of Trollbane. Prince Galen keeps the last sigil, which is needed to claim Trol'kalar. Prince Galen, son of Thoras Trollbane, keeps the last sigil in Stromgarde. He waits in a chapel deep in the districts held by the militia. Zengu warns that Galen is well guarded and a fine fighter. You are to kill the prince and carry the sigil back to Zengu in Hammerfall.

quest:645.text: Trol'kalar. At Stromgarde, Zengu sends you after Trol'kalar, now that four sigils have joined as one. Zengu has seen the four sigils unite as the Sigil of Ignaeus. He believes their union can break the wardings on Trollbane's tomb. The tomb lies in the Sanctum behind Stromgarde's chapel, and Zengu sends you there to retrieve Trol'kalar. A fenced path to the right of the chapel entrance descends to the crypt.

quest:646.text: Trol'kalar. At Trollbane's Tomb, Trol'kalar slips free of its stone sheath as the light fades. You carry the sword to Zengu in Hammerfall. At Trollbane's Tomb, you find Trol'kalar free of its stone sheath. You carry the sheathed sword to Zengu in Hammerfall, in the Arathi Highlands.

quest:648.text: Rescue OOX-17/TN!. At Steamwheedle Port, OOX-17/TN needs time and open ground for take-off. Oglethorpe's voice comes through the damaged robot, asking you to escort it there safely, then find him in Booty Bay. Oglethorpe's voice crackles through OOX-17/TN again. The robot has built-in cloaking, but Oglethorpe needs time to make it work again. It needs an open, safe place to begin its lengthy take-off. Oglethorpe has chosen Steamwheedle Port, and the journey there will give him time to restore the cloaking. You are asked to escort the robot safely. Once OOX-17/TN reaches Steamwheedle Port, find Oglethorpe Obnoticus in Booty Bay. He is a master inventor.

quest:652.text: Breaking the Keystone. The voice has more freedom now, though the Keystone still binds it. The Keystone lies among a ring of stones, and Fozruk holds the key the watchers call the Rod of Order. Opening the Stones of Binding eased the voice's confinement, but one lock still holds the Keystone. It lies among the circle of stones around you. Fozruk, a stone watcher and one of its captors, holds the key the watchers call the Rod of Order. Carry the rod to the Keystone and open the lock. The voice promises gratitude that will shake the earth to its roots. Geomantic energy fills the Keystone.

quest:653.text: Myzrael's Allies. Myzrael is free, yet she must gather strength before she can face her captors. She calls you a noble ally and sends you to Gerrig Bonegrip in a shop in Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern, where he knows how to summon her. Myzrael is free, but not strong enough to face her captors. They would overpower her now and lock her away again. So she will gather strength in hiding. When she is ready, she means to face the giants and make them rue the day they held her. She calls you a noble ally and says she will need your help to summon her to the surface. Myzrael sends you to Gerrig Bonegrip, whose shop is in Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern. He knows how to summon her.

quest:654.text:
Tanaris Field Sampling. In Tanaris, a field test begins as soon as the kit's power source is switched on. Your two hours of sampling start then. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle expected the kit to glow and vibrate once its power source was running. Now you have two hours to gather acceptable samples from eight basilisks, eight hyenas and eight scorpions in the Tanaris desert.

If the time runs out, all the data is lost. You will need to buy another power source from Bilgewhizzle, then return the kit to him in Gadgetzan before its power gives out. Bilgewhizzle offers no sympathy when a kit goes dead. The Gadgetzan Water Company’s profit is all that matters to him.

He will keep selling power sources until the company can afford to import water from the icy springs of Dun Morogh.

quest:656.text: Summoning the Princess. At the Shards of Myzrael, you summon Myzrael and face her before she grows strong enough to challenge her captors. Theldurin the Lost wants her defeated and her Eldritch Shackles bound to the Shards. Theldurin fears Myzrael will grow strong enough to turn against her captors. Some say she can be controlled. But Theldurin asks why the giants would have chained her if that were true. You take the Scroll of Myzrael to the Shards, where you first spoke with her, and call her forth. Once Myzrael is defeated, you bind her Eldritch Shackles to the Shards and trap her again.

quest:6568.text: The Testament of Rexxar. Rexxar sends you to the Western Plaguelands with a message for Myranda the Hag. He needs her skill with illusions to pass the Black Flight's defenses. Rexxar needs an illusion to pass the Black Flight's defenses. So he sends you to Myranda the Hag, a master illusionist who lives in the Western Plaguelands. The Lordaeron alliance drove her out. She has helped Rexxar's kind before, when a cause seemed worthy. Now you carry his message to her. A member of the Horde is a rare sight in these parts of Lordaeron, Myranda says. Then she asks what you have brought her.

quest:662.text: Deep Sea Salvage. After Land Ho!, First Mate Nilzlix asks you to recover the charts and logs from two wrecks before anyone leaves the cove. O'Breen brought three ships into the cove, certain treasure lay there. The Harbinger docked safely. But the Maiden's Folly and the Spirit of Silverpine reached the reef as the tides began to fall. Both struck a temple-like structure and sank fast. First Mate Nilzlix wants you to recover the logs and charts from both wrecks. He fears the information could reach prying eyes. If enemies found it, Fleet Master Seahorn would force the crew down the plank.

quest:664.text: Drowned Sorrows. At Faldir's Cove, Captain Steelgut mourns the Maiden's Folly and asks you to kill the Daggerspine naga who slew the wreck's survivors. At Faldir's Cove, Captain Steelgut sits by the fire and wishes the sea had taken him too. His crew fought hard to save the Maiden's Folly, but water rushed in all at once and the ship sank. O'Breen reached shore safely, while the naga killed the other survivors. Steelgut wants ten Daggerspine raiders and three Daggerspine sorceresses dead.

quest:665.text: Sunken Treasure. Professor Phizzlethorpe and Doctor Draxlegauge now aid the Blackwater Raiders in their search for lost elven treasure. Before the search can begin, the professor needs your protection while he charges goggles for the dark sea. Professor Phizzlethorpe asks you to guard him as he prepares for a search beneath the dark sea. Doctor Draxlegauge built goggles to find the lost gems, but they need power from an enchanted stone in a cave a short way uphill. The cave is cursed, and those who draw near are ambushed. Defend the professor while he draws the stone’s energy into the goggles.

quest:666.text: Sunken Treasure. In Faldir's Cove, Doctor Draxlegauge lends you his goggles to find ten elven gems for Captain O'Breen. He expects them back when you finish. The elven gems have lain on the sea floor so long that thick stone has hardened around them. The Goggles of Gem Hunting hold the power to find them through those stony shells. Proud of the gnomish ingenuity behind the goggles, Doctor Draxlegauge lends them to you. The gems are for Captain O'Breen. Doctor Draxlegauge says scientific work keeps him on safe, dry land, though he could swim down himself. He expects you to return the goggles afterward. Captain O'Breen, he says, will have plenty of use for them.

quest:667.text: Death From Below. Aboard Shakes O'Breen's ship in the Arathi Highlands, the Daggerspine naga gather to strike. You stand with O'Breen, man the cannon, and help the crew sail back to Booty Bay. After the Sunken Treasure, Shakes O'Breen sees the Daggerspine naga gathering to attack. They are ruthless and will keep coming until O'Breen is dead. O'Breen puts the crew's safety ahead of their own and asks you to defend them. Without O'Breen's knowledge of the seas, the crew cannot reach Booty Bay. So you wait aboard with O'Breen for the naga to rise from the water.

quest:668.text: Sunken Treasure. Doctor Draxlegauge sends you to Captain O'Breen, who waits at the bridge for the elven gems. After weeks among pirates, the doctor and the professor have learned that keeping pirate treasure is bad for their health. Doctor Draxlegauge is eager to bring Captain O'Breen the elven gems. The captain waits at the bridge and wants to see them for himself. After weeks among these pirates, the doctor and the professor have learned that keeping pirate treasure is bad for their health. So Draxlegauge gives you the gems to carry to O'Breen.

quest:669.text: Sunken Treasure. In Sunken Treasure, Shakes O'Breen is held back by the low tide and watchful creatures, so word must reach Booty Bay. Shakes O'Breen needs Fleet Master Seahorn in Booty Bay to hear of the find at once. The tide is too low for him to leave, and the creatures his crew disturbed watch every move. He asks you to tell Seahorn the treasure has been found and more is being brought up. You carry a sample elven gem as proof.

quest:670.text: Sunken Treasure. Fleet Master Seahorn waits in Booty Bay with a letter for Shakes O'Breen off the Arathi coast. His ships cannot sail until they restock. Fleet Master Seahorn sees an adventurer in you. His ships must restock before they can leave Booty Bay. Heavy things are brewing here and abroad, he says, and he has a secret letter for Shakes O'Breen off the Arathi coast. Can he trust you to deliver it safely and keep it confidential?

quest:673.text: Foul Magics. In Hammerfall, Tor'gan fears a warlock in Stromgarde is calling demons with an arcane relic. Your first work for him has led to a hunt for the warlock and the relic. Tor'gan is certain a warlock within Stromgarde's walls uses an arcane relic to call up terrible demons in great numbers. The burning in his blood grows by the day. So he sends you to find and kill the warlock, then bring back the magical object on the warlock's body. He means to destroy it before its power can taint the land. The warlock is Marez Cowl, and the object is a Befouled Bloodstone Orb.

quest:679.text: Call to Arms. At Hammerfall, Drum Fel sends you after the Boulderfist leaders in Stromgarde. After your earlier work, he says it is time to strike the head from the beast. Drum Fel says you are ready to help deliver one last great blow. The Boulderfist leaders have made their lair in Stromgarde’s ruins, which he calls a symbol of human frailty. He sends you to hunt down the lords and the shaman who serve them. They lead attacks meant to drive the Horde from these lands.

quest:680.text: The Real Threat. Korin Fel asks you to end the attacks on Hammerfall by slaying Or'Kalar and bringing her his head. Korin Fel says you serve her husband well, though he does not know why Hammerfall is under attack. Or'Kalar serves Mug'thol in Stromgarde and seeks her husband's death. Years ago, her husband defeated the ogre. Now Korin's auguries warn that Or'Kalar has set a trap for him. Korin has hidden the signs of Or'Kalar's presence from her husband. She fears he would rush off foolishly if he knew where the ogre was, so she asks you to help instead. Or'Kalar is near the Tower of Arathor. Korin expects his death to end the attacks on Hammerfall.

quest:687.text: Theldurin the Lost. In the Badlands, the Twilight's Hammer hunts for Theldurin the Lost and the scroll of Myzrael he took when he fled. Theldurin once followed the Twilight's Hammer. Then his mind slipped, and he turned from its teachings. He fled with the scroll of Myzrael, and the order could not catch him. Word has reached the Twilight's Hammer that Theldurin hides in the Badlands, raving and mad. The order needs the scroll for the Lady's return. First, you must find the man who took it.

quest:688.text: Myzrael's Allies. Through the keystone, Myzrael declares herself free, though still hidden from her captors. She sends you to Zaruk in Hammerfall, who knows how to summon her. Myzrael declares that she is free through the keystone. She must gather her strength out of sight. Her captors would overpower and imprison her again if they faced her now.
